title.zh: 卷一百七十九 列傳第一百二十九: 蕭遘 孔緯 韋昭度 崔昭緯 張濬 朱樸 鄭綮 劉崇望 徐彥若 陸扆 柳璨
title.en: Volume 179 Biographies 129: Xiao Gou, Kong Wei, Wei Zhaodu, Cui Zhaowei, Zhang Jun, Zhu Pu, Zheng Qi, Liu Chongwang, Xu Yanruo, Lu Yu, Liu Can
title.raw: 卷一百七十九 列傳第一百二十九: 蕭遘 孔緯 韋昭度 崔昭緯 張濬 朱樸 鄭綮 劉崇望 徐彥若 陸扆 柳璨 Volume 179 Biographies 129: Xiao Gou, Kong Wei, Wei Zhaodu, Cui Zhaowei, Zhang Jun, Zhu Pu, Zheng Qi, Liu Chongwang, Xu Yanruo, Lu Yu, Liu Can

sentences.zh: 蕭遘，蘭陵人。

translations.literal: Xiao Gou was a native of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gou came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 開元朝宰相太師徐國公嵩之四代孫。

translations.literal: He was the fourth-generation descendant of Song, Grand Tutor and Duke of Xu, who had served as chancellor in the Kaiyuan reign.
translations.idiomatic: He was a fourth-generation descendant of Xiao Song, Grand Tutor and Duke of Xu, who had served as chancellor during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 嵩生衡。

translations.literal: Song begot Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Song's son was Heng.

sentences.zh: 衡生復，德宗朝宰相。

translations.literal: Heng begot Fu, a chancellor in the Dezong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's son Fu served as chancellor under Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 復生湛。

translations.literal: Fu begot Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's son was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛生寘，咸通中宰相。

translations.literal: Zhan begot Zhi, a chancellor in the Xiantong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's son Zhi served as chancellor during the Xiantong period.

sentences.zh: 寘生遘，以登進士第，釋褐秘書省校書郎、太原從事。

translations.literal: Zhi begot Gou, who passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as proofreader in the Secretariat, and served as an aide in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Gou passed the jinshi examination, entered service as a proofreader in the Secretariat, and later served as an aide in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 入朝爲右拾遺，再遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Reminder and was twice promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Right Reminder and was promoted twice to become Recorder of the Emperor's Actions.

sentences.zh: 與韋保衡同年登進士第，保衡以幸進無藝，同年門生皆薄之。

translations.literal: He and Wei Baoheng passed the jinshi examination in the same year; Baoheng had risen through favor without talent, and their fellow graduates all looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wei Baoheng had passed the jinshi examination in the same year. Baoheng had risen through imperial favor without real ability, and their fellow graduates all held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 遘形神秀偉，志操不群。

translations.literal: Gou's bearing was handsome and imposing, and his will and conduct were uncommon.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was handsome and imposing in appearance, with a will and character that set him apart.

sentences.zh: 自比李德裕，同年皆戲呼「太尉」，保衡心銜之。

translations.literal: He compared himself to Li Deyu, and his classmates jokingly called him 'Grand Marshal'; Baoheng bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: He likened himself to Li Deyu, and his classmates jokingly called him 'Grand Marshal.' Baoheng nursed a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 及保衡作相，掎遘之失，貶爲播州司馬。

translations.literal: When Baoheng became chancellor, he seized on Gou's faults and had him demoted to assistant prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoheng became chancellor, he seized on Gou's faults and had him demoted to assistant prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 途經三峽，維舟月夜賦詩自悼。

translations.literal: Passing through the Three Gorges, he moored his boat on a moonlit night and composed a poem in self-lament.
translations.idiomatic: While passing through the Three Gorges, he moored his boat on a moonlit night and composed a poem lamenting his fate.

sentences.zh: 慮保衡見害，遽有神人謂之曰：「相公勿憂，予當禦侮奉衛。」

translations.literal: Fearing harm from Baoheng, suddenly a divine man said to him: 'Sir, do not worry. I shall ward off insult and guard you.'
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Baoheng would harm him, he suddenly heard a divine being say, "Sir, do not worry. I shall ward off insult and guard you."

sentences.zh: 遘心異之。

translations.literal: Gou was struck by the strangeness of it.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was deeply struck by the strangeness of the encounter.

sentences.zh: 過峽州，經白帝祠，即所睹之神人也。

translations.literal: Passing Xia Prefecture, he visited the Temple of the White Emperor and found it was the divine man he had seen.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed through Xia Prefecture and visited the Temple of the White Emperor, he found it was the same divine being he had seen before.

sentences.zh: 保衡誅，以禮部員外郎征還，轉考功員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: After Baoheng was executed, Gou was summoned back as vice minister of rites, then transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations and made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoheng was executed, Gou was recalled as vice minister of rites, then transferred to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations and appointed drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，召充翰林學士，正拜中書舍人，累遷戸部侍郎、翰林承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianfu reign he was summoned to serve as Hanlin academician, formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue and chief Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianfu era he was summoned to serve as a Hanlin academician, formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue and chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯闕，僖宗出幸，以供饋不給，須近臣掌計，改兵部侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital, Emperor Xizong fled, and because provisions were insufficient, a nearby minister was needed to manage accounts; Gou was changed to vice minister of war and put in charge of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao attacked the capital and Emperor Xizong fled, provisions ran short and a senior minister was needed to manage accounts. Gou was reassigned as vice minister of war and put in charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 三月，自褒中幸成都，次綿州。

translations.literal: In the third month, from Baozhong the emperor proceeded to Chengdu, stopping at Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor traveled from Baozhong to Chengdu, stopping at Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以本官同平章事，加中書侍郎，累兼吏部尚書、監修國史。

translations.literal: With his existing office he became co-chancellor, was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, and cumulatively held the posts of minister of civil affairs and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: With his existing office he became co-chancellor, was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, and cumulatively held the posts of minister of civil affairs and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 遘少負大節，以經濟爲己任。

translations.literal: From youth Gou bore great integrity and took statecraft as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Gou bore great integrity and took statecraft as his personal responsibility.

sentences.zh: 洎處臺司，風望尤峻，奏對朗拔，天子器之。

translations.literal: Once he held office in the censorate, his reputation was especially stern; in memorials and responses he was clear and forceful, and the Son of Heaven valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held office in the censorate, his reputation was especially stern. In memorials and responses he was clear and forceful, and the emperor valued him.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，王綱不振。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangqi reign, the imperial order was no longer upheld.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangqi era, the imperial order was no longer upheld.

sentences.zh: 是時天下諸侯，半出群盜；

translations.literal: At that time half the feudal lords of the realm had risen from bandit ranks;
translations.idiomatic: At that time half the feudal lords of the realm had risen from bandit ranks.

sentences.zh: 強弱相噬，怙眾邀寵，國法莫能制。

translations.literal: the strong devoured the weak, they relied on their numbers to demand favor, and national law could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The strong devoured the weak, relied on their numbers to demand favor, and national law could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 有李凝古者，從支詳爲徐州從事。

translations.literal: There was one Li Ninggu, who followed Zhi Xiang as an aide in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Li Ninggu who had served as an aide to Zhi Xiang in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詳爲衙將時溥所逐，而賓佐陷於徐。

translations.literal: When Xiang was driven out as a guard officer by Shi Pu, his staff were trapped in Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang was driven out by guard officer Shi Pu, his staff were trapped in Xu.

sentences.zh: 及溥爲節度使，因食中毒。

translations.literal: When Pu became military governor, he was poisoned while eating.
translations.idiomatic: After Pu became military governor, he was poisoned while eating.

sentences.zh: 而惡凝古者譖之，云爲支詳報讎行鴆。

translations.literal: Those who hated Ninggu slandered him, saying he had poisoned Pu to avenge Zhi Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hated Ninggu slandered him, claiming he had poisoned Pu to avenge Zhi Xiang.

sentences.zh: 溥收凝古殺之。

translations.literal: Pu arrested Ninggu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu arrested Ninggu and killed him.

sentences.zh: 凝古父損，時爲右常侍，溥上章披訴，言損與凝古同謀。

translations.literal: Ninggu's father Sun was then Right Regular Attendant; Pu submitted a memorial accusing Sun and Ninggu of plotting together.
translations.idiomatic: Ninggu's father Sun was then Right Regular Attendant. Pu submitted a memorial accusing Sun and Ninggu of plotting together.

sentences.zh: 內官田令孜受溥厚賂，曲奏請收損下獄。

translations.literal: The inner official Tian Lingzi accepted a heavy bribe from Pu and bent the memorial, asking that Sun be arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Tian Lingzi accepted a heavy bribe from Pu and bent the memorial, asking that Sun be arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 中丞盧渥附令孜，鍛煉其獄。

translations.literal: The vice censor Lu Wo sided with Lingzi and forged the case.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor Lu Wo sided with Lingzi and forged the case.

sentences.zh: 侍御史王華嫉惡，堅執奏證損無罪。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Wang Hua, who detested wrongdoing, firmly memorialized that Sun was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Wang Hua, who detested wrongdoing, firmly memorialized that Sun was innocent.

sentences.zh: 令孜怒，奏移損付神策獄按問，王華拒不奉詔，奏曰：「李損位居近侍，當死即死，安可取辱於黃門之手？」

translations.literal: Lingzi was angry and memorialized to transfer Sun to the Shence Army prison for interrogation; Wang Hua refused the edict and memorialized: 'Li Sun holds a post near the throne. If he must die, let him die—how can he be subjected to insult at the hands of eunuchs?'
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi was angry and memorialized to transfer Sun to the Shence Army prison for interrogation. Wang Hua refused the edict and memorialized, "Li Sun holds a post near the throne. If he must die, let him die—how can he be subjected to insult at the hands of eunuchs?"

sentences.zh: 遘非時進狀，請開延英，奏曰：「李凝古行鴆之謀，其事暖昧，已遭屠害，今不復論。

translations.literal: Gou submitted an untimely memorial asking to open the Yanying Hall and said: 'Li Ninggu's plot to poison is ambiguous in the facts, and he has already been slaughtered—let that not be discussed again.
translations.idiomatic: Gou submitted an untimely memorial asking to open the Yanying Hall and said, "Li Ninggu's alleged plot to poison is ambiguous in the facts, and he has already been slaughtered—let that not be discussed again.

sentences.zh: 李損父子相別三四年，音問斷絕，安得誣罔同謀？

translations.literal: Li Sun and his son had been apart three or four years with no word between them—how could they be falsely accused of plotting together?
translations.idiomatic: Li Sun and his son had been apart three or four years with no word between them—how could they be falsely accused of plotting together?

sentences.zh: 時溥恃勛壞法，淩蔑朝廷，而抗表請按侍臣，悖戾何甚？

translations.literal: Shi Pu relies on his merit to break the law and tramples the court—yet he submits a memorial demanding investigation of a serving minister. How perverse is this?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu relies on his merit to break the law and tramples the court—yet he submits a memorial demanding investigation of a serving minister. How perverse is this?

sentences.zh: 厚誣良善，人皆痛心。

translations.literal: He has deeply wronged the good and honest, and all hearts are pained.
translations.idiomatic: He has deeply wronged the good and honest, and all hearts are pained.

sentences.zh: 若李損羅織而誅，行當便及臣等。」

translations.literal: If Li Sun is framed and executed, the blow will soon reach us as well.'
translations.idiomatic: If Li Sun is framed and executed, the blow will soon reach us as well."

sentences.zh: 帝爲之改容，損得免，止於停任。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression changed, Sun was spared, and was only suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed. Sun was spared and only suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 時田令孜專總禁軍，公卿僚庶，無不候其顏色，唯遘以道自處，未嘗屈降。

translations.literal: At that time Tian Lingzi monopolized command of the imperial armies; nobles and officials all watched his mood—only Gou conducted himself by principle and never bowed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tian Lingzi monopolized command of the imperial armies. Nobles and officials all watched his mood—only Gou conducted himself by principle and never bowed.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，令孜奏安邑兩池鹽利，請直屬禁軍。

translations.literal: That winter Lingzi memorialized that the salt profits of the Anyi pools should be placed directly under the imperial armies.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Lingzi memorialized that the salt profits of the Anyi pools should be placed directly under the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 王重榮上章論列。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong submitted a memorial arguing the point.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong submitted a memorial arguing the point.

sentences.zh: 乃奏移重榮別鎮。

translations.literal: Lingzi then memorialized to transfer Chongrong to another command.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi then memorialized to transfer Chongrong to another command.

sentences.zh: 重榮不受，令孜請率禁軍討之。

translations.literal: Chongrong refused; Lingzi asked to lead the imperial armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong refused. Lingzi asked to lead the imperial armies to attack him.

sentences.zh: 重榮求援於太原，李克用引軍赴之，拒戰沙苑，禁軍大敗，逼京城。

translations.literal: Chongrong sought aid from Taiyuan; Li Keyong led troops to meet him. They fought at Shayuan; the imperial armies were greatly defeated and pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrong sought aid from Taiyuan. Li Keyong led troops to meet him. They fought at Shayuan; the imperial armies were greatly defeated and pressed the capital.

sentences.zh: 僖宗懼，出幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong was afraid and fled to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong was afraid and fled to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 諸籓上章抗論令孜生事，離間方面。

translations.literal: The feudal lords submitted memorials protesting that Lingzi was stirring trouble and driving the regions apart.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal lords submitted memorials protesting that Lingzi was stirring trouble and driving the regions apart.

sentences.zh: 遘素惡令孜，乃與裴澈致書召朱玫。

translations.literal: Gou had long hated Lingzi and therefore joined Pei Che in writing to summon Zhu Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Gou had long hated Lingzi and therefore joined Pei Che in writing to summon Zhu Mei.

sentences.zh: 玫以邠州之軍五千迎駕，仍與河中、太原修睦，請同匡王室。

translations.literal: Mei came with five thousand troops from Bin Prefecture to welcome the imperial carriage, and also made peace with Hezhong and Taiyuan, asking to restore the royal house together.
translations.idiomatic: Mei came with five thousand troops from Bin Prefecture to welcome the imperial carriage, made peace with Hezhong and Taiyuan, and asked to restore the royal house together.

sentences.zh: 由是，諸鎮繼上章，請駕還京。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commands in succession submitted memorials asking the carriage to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the commands in succession submitted memorials asking the imperial carriage to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 令孜聞玫軍至，迫脅天子幸陳倉。

translations.literal: When Lingzi heard Mei's army had arrived, he forced the Son of Heaven to proceed to Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzi heard Mei's army had arrived, he forced the emperor to proceed to Chencang.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗倉卒出城，夜中百官不及扈從。

translations.literal: The emperor had left the city in haste; in the night the officials could not accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had left the city in haste. In the night the officials could not accompany him.

sentences.zh: 玫怒令孜弄權，又以天子不諒其忠，語辭怨望，乃訴於遘曰：「主上六年奔播，百端艱險。

translations.literal: Mei was angry that Lingzi manipulated power, and also that the Son of Heaven did not trust his loyalty; his words were resentful, and he complained to Gou: 'For six years the sovereign has wandered in exile amid every hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Mei was angry that Lingzi manipulated power and that the emperor did not trust his loyalty. His words were resentful, and he complained to Gou, "For six years the sovereign has wandered in exile amid every hardship.

sentences.zh: 中原士庶，與賊血戰，肝腦塗地，十室九空。

translations.literal: The gentry of the central plains fought the bandits to the death; blood and brains smeared the ground, and nine of ten households were empty.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry of the central plains fought the bandits to the death. Blood and brains smeared the ground, and nine of ten households were empty.

sentences.zh: 比至收復京都，十亡七八。

translations.literal: By the time the capital was recovered, seven or eight in ten were gone.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the capital was recovered, seven or eight in ten were gone.

sentences.zh: 殘民遺老，方喜車駕歸宮。

translations.literal: The surviving people and aged remnant were just rejoicing that the imperial carriage would return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The surviving people and aged remnant were just rejoicing that the imperial carriage would return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 主上不念生靈轉輸之勞，甲士血戰之效，將勤王之功業，爲敕使之寵榮；

translations.literal: The sovereign does not consider the toil of transporting the living, the blood shed by armored soldiers, or the merit of those who aided the throne—he turns the achievement of loyal service into favor for his commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign does not consider the toil of transporting the living, the blood shed by armored soldiers, or the merit of those who aided the throne—he turns the achievement of loyal service into favor for his commissioners.

sentences.zh: 而更志在亂邦，與國生事，召戎結怨，不自他人。

translations.literal: rather he still aims to disorder the state, stir trouble for the realm, summon enemies and breed resentment—not from others, but from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Rather he still aims to disorder the state, stir trouble for the realm, summon enemies and breed resentment—not from others, but from himself.

sentences.zh: 昨奉指蹤，徑來奔問，不蒙見信，翻類脅君。

translations.literal: Yesterday, obeying orders, I came directly to inquire after you, yet was not trusted and seemed instead to coerce the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, obeying orders, I came directly to inquire after you, yet was not trusted and seemed instead to coerce the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 古者忠而獲罪，正如此也！

translations.literal: In antiquity loyalty that earned punishment was just like this!
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity loyalty that earned punishment was just like this!

sentences.zh: 吾等報國之心極矣！

translations.literal: Our hearts in serving the state are at their limit!
translations.idiomatic: Our hearts in serving the state are at their limit!

sentences.zh: 戰賊之力殫矣！

translations.literal: Our strength in fighting the bandits is exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: Our strength in fighting the bandits is exhausted!

sentences.zh: 安能垂頭疊翼，喘喘於閽寺之手哉！

translations.literal: How can we hang our heads and fold our wings, gasping in the hands of gatekeepers!
translations.idiomatic: How can we hang our heads and fold our wings, gasping in the hands of gatekeepers!

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，喪君有君。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is: when the ruler is lost, there is still a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is: when the ruler is lost, there is still a ruler.

sentences.zh: 相國徐思其宜，改圖可也。」

translations.literal: Chancellor, consider what is fitting and change course.'
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor, consider what is fitting and change course."

sentences.zh: 遘曰：「主上臨御十餘年，未聞過行。

translations.literal: Gou said: 'The sovereign has ruled more than ten years, and no misconduct has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Gou said, "The sovereign has ruled more than ten years, and no misconduct has been heard.

sentences.zh: 比來喪亂播越，失於授任非才。

translations.literal: The recent scattering in chaos came from appointing the unfit.
translations.idiomatic: The recent scattering in chaos came from appointing the unfit.

sentences.zh: 近年令孜掣肘，動不如意，上每言之，流涕不已。

translations.literal: In recent years Lingzi has checked every move; nothing goes as wished. The sovereign speaks of it often, weeping without end.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Lingzi has checked every move; nothing goes as wished. The sovereign speaks of it often, weeping without end.

sentences.zh: 昨去陳倉，上無行意，令孜陳兵帳下，列卒階前，造次迫行，不容俟旦。

translations.literal: When he left Chencang the sovereign had no wish to go; Lingzi arrayed troops below his tent and lined soldiers before the steps, forcing him to depart at once without waiting for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: When he left Chencang the sovereign had no wish to go. Lingzi arrayed troops below his tent and lined soldiers before the steps, forcing him to depart at once without waiting for dawn.

sentences.zh: 靜言此賊，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Reflect on this villain—his crimes admit no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Reflect on this villain—his crimes admit no punishment.

sentences.zh: 至尊之心，孰不深鑒？

translations.literal: Who in the sovereign's heart does not see it clearly?
translations.idiomatic: Who in the sovereign's heart does not see it clearly?

sentences.zh: 足下乃心王室，止有歸兵還鎮，拜表迎鑾，德業功名，益光圖史。

translations.literal: You are loyal to the royal house; you need only return your troops to your command, submit a memorial welcoming the imperial carriage, and your merit and fame will shine brighter in history.
translations.idiomatic: You are loyal to the royal house. You need only return your troops to your command, submit a memorial welcoming the imperial carriage, and your merit and fame will shine brighter in history.

sentences.zh: 舍此已往；

translations.literal: Beyond that;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that—

sentences.zh: 理或未安。

translations.literal: the principle may not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: the principle may not be secure.

sentences.zh: 改圖之言，未敢聞命。」

translations.literal: I dare not hear talk of changing course.'
translations.idiomatic: I dare not hear talk of changing course."

sentences.zh: 玫曰：「李家王子極多，有天下者，豈一王哉？」

translations.literal: Mei said: 'The Li house has very many princes. Is there only one king who can hold the realm?'
translations.idiomatic: Mei said, "The Li house has very many princes. Is there only one king who can hold the realm?"

sentences.zh: 遘曰：「廢立危事，雖有伊尹、霍光之賢，尚貽後悔。

translations.literal: Gou said: 'Deposing and enthroning is a perilous matter. Even with the worth of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, regret still follows.
translations.idiomatic: Gou said, "Deposing and enthroning is a perilous matter. Even with the worth of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, regret still follows.

sentences.zh: 古人云：『勿爲福始，勿爲禍先。』

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Do not be the first to seek fortune; do not be the first to invite disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'Do not be the first to seek fortune; do not be the first to invite disaster.'

sentences.zh: 如公矢謀，未見其利。」

translations.literal: In the plan you propose, I see no benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: In the plan you propose, I see no benefit."

sentences.zh: 玫退而宣言曰：「我冊個王子爲主，不從者斬。」

translations.literal: Mei withdrew and proclaimed: 'I will enthrone a prince as sovereign. Whoever does not obey will be beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: Mei withdrew and proclaimed, "I will enthrone a prince as sovereign. Whoever does not obey will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 及立襄王，請遘爲冊文。

translations.literal: When the Xiang Prince was enthroned, Mei asked Gou to draft the enthronement text.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiang Prince was enthroned, Mei asked Gou to draft the enthronement text.

sentences.zh: 遘曰：「少嬰衰疾，文思減落。

translations.literal: Gou said: 'From youth I have been weak and ill; my literary thought has declined.
translations.idiomatic: Gou said, "From youth I have been weak and ill; my literary thought has declined.

sentences.zh: 比來禁署，未免倩人，請命能者。」

translations.literal: Lately in the forbidden secretariat I have had to borrow others' work. Please order someone capable.'
translations.idiomatic: Lately in the forbidden secretariat I have had to borrow others' work. Please order someone capable."

sentences.zh: 竟不措筆。

translations.literal: He never put brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: He never put brush to paper.

sentences.zh: 乃命鄭昌圖爲之，玫滋不悅。

translations.literal: Zheng Changtu was ordered to do it, and Mei grew more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Changtu was ordered to do it, and Mei grew more displeased.

sentences.zh: 及還長安，以昌圖代遘爲相，署遘太子太保。

translations.literal: When they returned to Chang'an, Changtu replaced Gou as chancellor and Gou was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned to Chang'an, Changtu replaced Gou as chancellor and Gou was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 乃移疾，滿百日，退居河中之永樂縣。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness; after a hundred days he retired to Yongle County in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness. After a hundred days he retired to Yongle County in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 遘在相位五年，累兼尚書右僕射，進封楚國公。

translations.literal: Gou had been chancellor five years, cumulatively held Right Vice Director of the Department of State, and was advanced to Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Gou had been chancellor for five years, cumulatively held the post of Right Vice Director of the Department of State, and was advanced to Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 僖宗再遷京，宰相孔緯與遘不協，以其受偽命，奏貶官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong moved the capital again, Chancellor Kong Wei was at odds with Gou and memorialized to demote him for accepting a false appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong moved the capital again, Chancellor Kong Wei was at odds with Gou and memorialized to demote him for accepting a false appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋賜死於永樂。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to die at Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to die at Yongle.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，王鐸掌貢籍，遘與韋保衡俱以進士中選，而保衡暴貴，與鐸同在中書。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong reign Wang Duo managed the examination rolls; Gou and Wei Baoheng both passed the jinshi, and Baoheng rose violently, serving with Duo in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong reign Wang Duo managed the examination rolls. Gou and Wei Baoheng both passed the jinshi, and Baoheng rose violently, serving with Duo in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及僖宗在蜀，遘又與鐸並居相位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong was in Shu, Gou again served as chancellor alongside Duo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong was in Shu, Gou again served as chancellor alongside Duo.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗召宰臣，鐸年高，升階足跌，踣勾陳中，遘旁掖起，帝目之，喜曰：「輔弼之臣和，予之幸也。」

translations.literal: The emperor once summoned the chief ministers. Duo was old; climbing the steps his foot slipped and he fell in the Gouchen hall. Gou helped him up from the side. The emperor looked and said with pleasure: 'The assisting ministers are in harmony—this is my fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once summoned the chief ministers. Duo was old; climbing the steps his foot slipped and he fell in the Gouchen hall. Gou helped him up from the side. The emperor looked and said with pleasure, "The assisting ministers are in harmony—this is my fortune."

sentences.zh: 謂遘曰：「適見卿扶王鐸，予喜卿善事長矣。」

translations.literal: He said to Gou: 'Just now I saw you support Wang Duo. I am pleased that you know how to honor elders.'
translations.idiomatic: He said to Gou, "Just now I saw you support Wang Duo. I am pleased that you know how to honor elders."

sentences.zh: 遘對曰：「臣扶王鐸不獨司長。

translations.literal: Gou replied: 'In supporting Wang Duo I was not only honoring an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Gou replied, "In supporting Wang Duo I was not only honoring an elder.

sentences.zh: 臣應舉歲，鐸爲主司，以臣中選門生也。」

translations.literal: In the year I took the examination, Duo was chief examiner and I was his selected graduate.'
translations.idiomatic: In the year I took the examination, Duo was chief examiner and I was his selected graduate."

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「王鐸選進士，朕選宰相，於卿無負矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: 'Wang Duo selected a jinshi; I selected a chancellor. I have not failed you.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Wang Duo selected a jinshi; I selected a chancellor. I have not failed you."

sentences.zh: 遘謝之而退。

translations.literal: Gou thanked him and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gou thanked him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遘爲大臣，士行無缺。

translations.literal: As a great minister, Gou's conduct was without flaw.
translations.idiomatic: As a great minister, Gou's conduct was without flaw.

sentences.zh: 逢時不幸，爲偽襜所汙，不以令終，人士惜之。

translations.literal: He met an unlucky time and was stained by a false robe; he did not end well, and scholars regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He met an unlucky time and was stained by a false appointment. He did not end well, and scholars regretted it.

sentences.zh: 弟蘧，時爲永樂令。

translations.literal: His younger brother Su was then magistrate of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Su was then magistrate of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 孔緯，字化文，魯曲阜人，宣尼之裔。

translations.literal: Kong Wei, style name Huawen, was a native of Qufu in Lu, a descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei, whose courtesy name was Huawen, came from Qufu in Lu and was a descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 曾祖岑父，位終秘書省著作佐郎，諫議大夫巢父兄也。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Cenfu served to Secretariat Proofreader of Writings; he was the elder brother of Remonstrating Official Chaofu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Cenfu served as Proofreader of Writings in the Secretariat; he was the elder brother of Remonstrating Official Chaofu.

sentences.zh: 祖戣，位終禮部尚書，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kui served to Minister of Rites and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kui rose to Minister of Rites and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 父遵孺，終華陰縣丞。

translations.literal: His father Zunru served to assistant magistrate of Huayin County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zunru served as assistant magistrate of Huayin County.

sentences.zh: 緯少孤，依諸父溫裕、溫業，皆居方鎮，與名公交，故緯聲籍早達，

translations.literal: Wei was orphaned young and relied on his uncles Wenyu and Wenye, who both held regional commands and associated with famous men; thus Wei's reputation was early known.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was orphaned young and relied on his uncles Wenyu and Wenye, who both held regional commands and associated with famous men. Thus Wei's reputation spread early.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and took his first office as proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and took his first office as proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 崔慎由鎮梓州，辟爲從事。

translations.literal: When Cui Shenyou governed Zizhou, Wei was recruited as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Shenyou governed Zizhou, Wei was recruited as an aide.

sentences.zh: 又從崔鉉爲揚州支使，得協律郎。

translations.literal: He again followed Cui Xuan as branch secretary in Yangzhou and received the post of Coordinator of Music.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Cui Xuan as branch secretary in Yangzhou and received the post of Coordinator of Music.

sentences.zh: 崔慎由鎮華州、河中，緯皆從之，歷觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Cui Shenyou governed Hua and Hezhong, Wei followed him and served as investigating adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Shenyou governed Hua and Hezhong, Wei followed him and served as investigating adjutant.

sentences.zh: 宰相楊收奏授長安尉，直弘文館。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yang Shou memorialized him as magistrate of Chang'an and direct scholar of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yang Shou memorialized him as magistrate of Chang'an and direct scholar of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王鐸奏爲監察御史，轉禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Vice censor Wang Duo memorialized him as investigating censor, then transferred him to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor Wang Duo memorialized him as investigating censor, then transferred him to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 宰相徐商奏兼集賢直學士，改考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Chancellor Xu Shang memorialized him as concurrent direct scholar of the Jixian Institute and changed him to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xu Shang memorialized him as concurrent direct scholar of the Jixian Institute and changed him to vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 丁內憂免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed on mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，以右司員外郎入朝。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he entered court as vice director of the Bureau of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he entered court as vice director of the Bureau of the Right.

sentences.zh: 宰臣趙隱嘉其能文，薦爲翰林學士，轉考功郎中、知制誥，賜緋。

translations.literal: Chief minister Zhao Yin admired his literary ability and recommended him as Hanlin academician; he was transferred to director of the Bureau of Evaluations and drafter of edicts, and given crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhao Yin admired his literary ability and recommended him as Hanlin academician. He was transferred to director of the Bureau of Evaluations and drafter of edicts, and given crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 正拜中書舍人，累遷戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 謝日，面賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: On the day of thanksgiving he was personally given gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of thanksgiving he was personally given gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，罷學士，出爲御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu reign he was removed from the academy and sent out as vice censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era he was removed from the academy and sent out as vice censor.

sentences.zh: 緯器志方雅，嫉惡如仇。

translations.literal: Wei's capacity and will were upright and elegant; he hated evil as if it were a personal enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's capacity and will were upright and elegant. He hated evil as if it were a personal enemy.

sentences.zh: 既總憲綱，中外不繩而自肅。

translations.literal: Once he held the censorial reins, inside and outside the court were disciplined without needing the lash.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the censorial reins, inside and outside the court were disciplined without needing the lash.

sentences.zh: 歷戸部、兵部、吏部三侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the three vice ministries of revenue, war, and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the three vice ministries of revenue, war, and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 居選曹，動循格令。

translations.literal: In the Bureau of Appointments he always followed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the Bureau of Appointments he always followed the regulations.

sentences.zh: 權要有所托，私書盈幾，不之省。

translations.literal: When powerful men had requests, private letters filled his desk and he did not read them.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful men had requests, private letters filled his desk and he did not read them.

sentences.zh: 執政怒之，改太常卿。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were angry and changed him to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were angry and changed him to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之亂，從僖宗幸蜀，改刑部尚書，判戸部事。

translations.literal: In Huang Chao's rebellion he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu, was changed to Minister of Punishments, and put in charge of revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Huang Chao's rebellion he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu, was changed to Minister of Punishments, and put in charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 宰臣蕭遘在翰林時，與緯情旨不協。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Xiao Gou was in the Hanlin, he and Wei were not in accord in purpose.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Xiao Gou was in the Hanlin, he and Wei were not in accord in purpose.

sentences.zh: 至是，因戸部取給不充，移之散秩，改太子少保，

translations.literal: At this time, because revenue supplies were insufficient, Wei was moved to a nominal post as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent,
translations.idiomatic: At this time, because revenue supplies were insufficient, Wei was moved to a nominal post as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent,

sentences.zh: 從駕還京。

translations.literal: and followed the carriage back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: and followed the carriage back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，田令孜軍敗，沙陁逼京師，帝移幸鳳翔，邠帥朱玫引兵來迎駕。

translations.literal: At that time Tian Lingzi's army was defeated; the Shatuo pressed the capital; the emperor moved to Fengxiang; Bin commander Zhu Mei led troops to welcome the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tian Lingzi's army was defeated, the Shatuo pressed the capital, and the emperor moved to Fengxiang. Bin commander Zhu Mei led troops to welcome the carriage.

sentences.zh: 令孜挾帝幸山南。

translations.literal: Lingzi forced the emperor to proceed to Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi forced the emperor to proceed to Shannan.

sentences.zh: 時中夜出幸，百官不及扈從，而隨駕者黃門衛士數百人而已。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night the emperor departed; officials could not accompany him, and only a few hundred eunuch guards followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the night the emperor departed. Officials could not accompany him, and only a few hundred eunuch guards followed.

sentences.zh: 帝駐寶雞，侯百官，詔授緯御史大夫，遣中使傳詔，令緯率百僚赴行在。

translations.literal: The emperor halted at Baoji and waited for officials; he decreed Wei Censor-in-Chief and sent an inner envoy with the edict ordering Wei to lead the hundred officials to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted at Baoji and waited for officials. He decreed Wei Censor-in-Chief and sent an inner envoy with the edict ordering Wei to lead the hundred officials to the temporary court.

sentences.zh: 時京師急變，從駕官屬至盩厔，並爲亂兵所剽，資裝殆盡。

translations.literal: The capital was in sudden crisis; officials following the carriage reached Zhouzhi and were all plundered by mutinous soldiers until their goods were nearly gone.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was in sudden crisis. Officials following the carriage reached Zhouzhi and were all plundered by mutinous soldiers until their goods were nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 緯承命見宰相論事，蕭遘、裴澈以田令孜在帝左右，意不欲行，辭疾不見緯。

translations.literal: Wei received the order and went to see the chancellors to discuss affairs; Xiao Gou and Pei Che, because Tian Lingzi was at the emperor's side, did not wish to go and excused themselves on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei received the order and went to see the chancellors to discuss affairs. Xiao Gou and Pei Che, because Tian Lingzi was at the emperor's side, did not wish to go and excused themselves on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 緯遣臺吏促百官上路，皆以袍笏不具爲詞。

translations.literal: Wei sent censorial clerks to urge the hundred officials onto the road; all pleaded that robes and tablets were not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent censorial clerks to urge the hundred officials onto the road. All pleaded that robes and tablets were not complete.

sentences.zh: 緯無如之何，乃召三院御史謂之曰：「吾輩世荷國恩，身居憲秩。

translations.literal: Wei could do nothing and therefore summoned the three bureaus of censors and said: 'Our generations have received national grace, and we hold censorial rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wei could do nothing and therefore summoned the three bureaus of censors and said, "Our generations have received national grace, and we hold censorial rank.

sentences.zh: 雖六飛奔迫而咫尺天顏，累詔追征，皆無承稟，非臣子之義也。

translations.literal: Though the six regalia flee in haste, the imperial countenance is within a foot; repeated edicts summon us, yet none respond—this is not the duty of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Though the six regalia flee in haste, the imperial countenance is within a foot. Repeated edicts summon us, yet none respond—this is not the duty of subjects.

sentences.zh: 凡布衣交舊，緩急猶相救恤，況在君親？

translations.literal: Even among common friends, in urgency they still aid one another—how much more under ruler and parent?
translations.idiomatic: Even among common friends, in urgency they still aid one another—how much more under ruler and parent?

sentences.zh: 策名委質，安可背也！」

translations.literal: Having pledged one's name and entrusted one's person, how can one turn away!'
translations.idiomatic: Having pledged one's name and entrusted one's person, how can one turn away!"

sentences.zh: 言竟泣下。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he wept.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking he wept.

sentences.zh: 三院曰：「夫豈不懷，但盩厔剽剝之餘，乞食不給。

translations.literal: The three bureaus said: 'Who would not wish it? But after the plunder at Zhouzhi we cannot even beg food.
translations.idiomatic: The three bureaus said, "Who would not wish it? But after the plunder at Zhouzhi we cannot even beg food.

sentences.zh: 今若首途，聊營一日之費，俟信宿紀行可也。」

translations.literal: If we set out now, we can barely gather one day's expenses; wait a night or two and then travel.'
translations.idiomatic: If we set out now, we can barely gather one day's expenses. Wait a night or two and then travel."

sentences.zh: 緯拂衣起曰：「吾妻危疾，旦不保夕，丈夫豈以妻子之故，怠君父之急乎？

translations.literal: Wei brushed his robes and rose: 'My wife is gravely ill and may not survive the day. Would a man, for wife and children, neglect the urgency of ruler and father?
translations.idiomatic: Wei brushed his robes and rose. "My wife is gravely ill and may not survive the day. Would a man, for wife and children, neglect the urgency of ruler and father?

sentences.zh: 公輩善自爲謀，吾行決矣。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen plan for yourselves—I am resolved to go.'
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen plan for yourselves—I am resolved to go."

sentences.zh: 即日見李昌符告曰：「主上再有詔命，令促百僚前進。

translations.literal: That day he saw Li Changfu and said: 'The sovereign has again decreed, urging the hundred officials forward.
translations.idiomatic: That day he saw Li Changfu and said, "The sovereign has again decreed, urging the hundred officials forward.

sentences.zh: 觀群公立意，未有發期。

translations.literal: Seeing the group's intent, none has a date of departure.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the group's intent, none has a date of departure.

sentences.zh: 僕忝憲闈，不宜居後。

translations.literal: I am shamed to hold the censorial gate and should not lag behind.
translations.idiomatic: I am shamed to hold the censorial gate and should not lag behind.

sentences.zh: 道途多梗，明公幸假五十騎，送至陳倉。」

translations.literal: The roads are blocked; may Your Excellency lend fifty riders to escort me to Chencang.'
translations.idiomatic: The roads are blocked. May Your Excellency lend fifty riders to escort me to Chencang."

sentences.zh: 昌符嘉之，謂緯曰：「路無頓遞，裹糧辦耶？」

translations.literal: Changfu admired this and said to Wei: 'There are no relay stations on the road—have you packed provisions?'
translations.idiomatic: Changfu admired this and said to Wei, "There are no relay stations on the road—have you packed provisions?"

sentences.zh: 乃送錢五十緡，令騎士援緯達散關。

translations.literal: He then sent fifty strings of cash and ordered horsemen to escort Wei to San Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent fifty strings of cash and ordered horsemen to escort Wei to San Pass.

sentences.zh: 緯知朱玫必蓄異志，奏曰：「關城小邑，不足以駐六師，請速幸梁州。」

translations.literal: Wei knew Zhu Mei must harbor rebellious intent and memorialized: 'This pass town is too small to station the six armies. Please proceed quickly to Liang Prefecture.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei knew Zhu Mei must harbor rebellious intent and memorialized, "This pass town is too small to station the six armies. Please proceed quickly to Liang Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 翌日，車駕離陳倉，才入關而邠、岐之兵圍寶雞，攻散關。

translations.literal: The next day the imperial carriage left Chencang; it had just entered the pass when Bin and Qi troops surrounded Baoji and attacked San Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the imperial carriage left Chencang. It had just entered the pass when Bin and Qi troops surrounded Baoji and attacked San Pass.

sentences.zh: 微緯之言幾危矣！

translations.literal: But for Wei's words, danger was nearly upon them!
translations.idiomatic: But for Wei's words, danger was nearly upon them!

sentences.zh: 至褒中，改兵部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，尋改中書侍郎、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: At Baozhong he was changed to vice minister of war and co-chancellor; soon he was changed to vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Baozhong he was changed to vice minister of war and co-chancellor. Soon he was changed to vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜斬朱玫，平定京城，遷門下侍郎、監修國史。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu beheaded Zhu Mei and pacified the capital; Wei was moved to vice director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu beheaded Zhu Mei and pacified the capital. Wei was moved to vice director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 從駕還京，駐蹕岐陽，進階特進，兼吏部尚書，領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Following the carriage back to the capital, the court halted at Qiyang; Wei was advanced to Special Advancement and concurrently Minister of Civil Affairs, and made commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Following the carriage back to the capital, the court halted at Qiyang. Wei was advanced to Special Advancement and concurrently Minister of Civil Affairs, and made commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，進位左僕射，賜「持危啟運保乂功臣」，食邑四千戸，食實封二百戸，賜鐵券，恕十死罪，賜天興縣莊、善和里宅各一區，兼領京畿營田使。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned to the palace, he was promoted to Left Vice Director, given the title 'Meritorious Minister Who Sustained Peril, Opened Fortune, and Preserved Order,' a fief of four thousand households with two hundred actual, an iron tally forgiving ten capital crimes, estates in Tianxing County and a mansion in Shanhe Lane, and concurrently made commissioner of capital-region military farms.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage returned to the palace, he was promoted to Left Vice Director, given the title 'Meritorious Minister Who Sustained Peril, Opened Fortune, and Preserved Order,' a fief of four thousand households with two hundred actual, an iron tally forgiving ten capital crimes, estates in Tianxing County and a mansion in Shanhe Lane, and concurrently made commissioner of capital-region military farms.

sentences.zh: 僖宗晏駕，充山陵使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong died, Wei served as commissioner of the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong died, Wei served as commissioner of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 僖宗祔廟，緯準故事，不入朝。

translations.literal: When Xizong was enshrined, Wei by precedent did not enter court.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong was enshrined, Wei by precedent did not enter court.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遣中使召赴延英，令緯依舊視事，進加司空。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong sent an inner envoy to summon him to Yanying and ordered him to resume duties as before; he was further promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong sent an inner envoy to summon him to Yanying and ordered him to resume duties as before. He was further promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以國學盜火所焚，令緯完葺，仍兼領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Because the imperial academy was burned by thieves, Zhaozong ordered Wei to repair it and also made him Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Because the imperial academy was burned by thieves, Zhaozong ordered Wei to repair it and also made him Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊秦宗權伏誅，進階開府儀同三司，進位司徒，封魯國公。

translations.literal: When the Cai bandit Qin Zongquan was executed, Wei was advanced to Grand General of the Palace Guard and promoted to Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cai bandit Qin Zongquan was executed, Wei was advanced to Grand General of the Palace Guard and promoted to Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，昭宗謁郊廟，兩中尉、內樞密請朝服。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhaozong visited the suburban altars; the two commanders of the palace armies and the Bureau of Inner Affairs requested court robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhaozong visited the suburban altars. The two commanders of the palace armies and the Bureau of Inner Affairs requested court robes.

sentences.zh: 所司申前例，中貴人無朝服助祭之禮，少府監亦無素制冠服。

translations.literal: The office cited precedent: inner favorites had no ritual of assisting sacrifice in court robes, and the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories had no plain-made caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: The office cited precedent: inner favorites had no ritual of assisting sacrifice in court robes, and the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories had no plain-made caps and robes.

sentences.zh: 中尉怒，立令制造，下太常禮院。

translations.literal: The commanders were angry and immediately ordered them made, sending the matter to the Ritual Court of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders were angry and immediately ordered them made, sending the matter to the Ritual Court of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 禮官舉故事，亦稱無中尉朝服助祭之文，諫官亦論之。

translations.literal: Ritual officials cited precedent and also said there was no text on commanders in court robes assisting sacrifice; remonstrating officials argued as well.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials cited precedent and also said there was no text on commanders in court robes assisting sacrifice. Remonstrating officials argued as well.

sentences.zh: 緯奏曰：「中貴不衣朝服助祭，國典也。

translations.literal: Wei memorialized: 'For inner favorites not to wear court robes in assisting sacrifice is national statute.
translations.idiomatic: Wei memorialized, "For inner favorites not to wear court robes in assisting sacrifice is national statute.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲以權道寵內臣，則請依所兼之官而爲之服。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes by expedient to favor inner ministers, then please have them wear robes according to the offices they concurrently hold.'
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes by expedient to favor inner ministers, then please have them wear robes according to the offices they concurrently hold."

sentences.zh: 天子召諫官謂之曰：「大禮日近，無宜立異，爲朕容之。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven summoned remonstrating officials and said: 'The great rite is near; there should be no needless dispute. Indulge me.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned remonstrating officials and said, "The great rite is near. There should be no needless dispute. Indulge me."

sentences.zh: 於是內官以朝服助祭。

translations.literal: Thereupon the inner officials assisted sacrifice in court robes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the inner officials assisted sacrifice in court robes.

sentences.zh: 郊禮畢，進位兼太保。

translations.literal: When the suburban rite was complete, Wei was promoted to concurrent Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When the suburban rite was complete, Wei was promoted to concurrent Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 延英中謝，奏曰：「臣前時待罪宰相，智術短淺，有負弼諧。

translations.literal: In Yanying he gave thanks and memorialized: 'Before, when I served as chancellor at fault, my wisdom was short and shallow and I failed in harmonizing assistance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanying he gave thanks and memorialized, "Before, when I served as chancellor at fault, my wisdom was short and shallow and I failed in harmonizing assistance.

sentences.zh: 陛下特貸刑書，曲全腰領。

translations.literal: Your Majesty specially spared the penal code and wholly preserved my neck.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty specially spared the penal code and wholly preserved my neck.

sentences.zh: 臣期於死報泉壤，不望生叩玉階。

translations.literal: I expected to repay in death beneath the springs and did not hope to live and kneel on the jade steps.
translations.idiomatic: I expected to repay in death beneath the springs and did not hope to live and kneel on the jade steps.

sentences.zh: 復拜龍顏，實臣榮幸。

translations.literal: To again behold the dragon countenance is truly my honor.
translations.idiomatic: To again behold the dragon countenance is truly my honor.

sentences.zh: 然臣比嬰衰疾，伏枕累年，形骸雖存，生意都盡。

translations.literal: Yet lately I have been weak and ill, lying on a pillow for years; though the body remains, all vital intent is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately I have been weak and ill, lying on a pillow for years. Though the body remains, all vital intent is gone.

sentences.zh: 平居勉強，禦事猶疏。

translations.literal: In ordinary times I force myself, yet in handling affairs I am still remiss.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times I force myself, yet in handling affairs I am still remiss.

sentences.zh: 況比尪羸，寧勝重委？

translations.literal: How much less now, when I am frail and weak, can I bear heavy commission?
translations.idiomatic: How much less now, when I am frail and weak, can I bear heavy commission?

sentences.zh: 國祚方泰，英彥盈庭，豈以朽腐之人，再塵機務！

translations.literal: The dynastic fortune is just flourishing and talented men fill the court—how can a rotting man again soil state affairs!
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic fortune is just flourishing and talented men fill the court—how can a rotting man again soil state affairs!

sentences.zh: 臣力疾一拜殿庭，乞陛下許臣自便。」

translations.literal: Though ill I bow once in the hall court; I beg Your Majesty to allow me to retire.'
translations.idiomatic: Though ill I bow once in the hall court. I beg Your Majesty to allow me to retire."

sentences.zh: 因鳴咽流涕。

translations.literal: He sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He sobbed and wept.

sentences.zh: 緯久疾，拜蹈艱難，上令中使止之，改容軫念。

translations.literal: Wei had long been ill; bowing and prostrating were difficult. The emperor ordered an inner envoy to stop him and changed his expression in pity.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had long been ill; bowing and prostrating were difficult. The emperor ordered an inner envoy to stop him and changed his expression in pity.

sentences.zh: 令閣門使送緯中書視事。

translations.literal: He ordered the Gate Commissioner to send Wei to the Secretariat to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Gate Commissioner to send Wei to the Secretariat to handle affairs.

sentences.zh: 不旬日，沙陁次河中，同州王行約入京師謀亂，天子出幸石門。

translations.literal: Within ten days the Shatuo halted at Hezhong; Wang Xingyue of Tong Prefecture entered the capital plotting rebellion, and the Son of Heaven fled to Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the Shatuo halted at Hezhong. Wang Xingyue of Tong Prefecture entered the capital plotting rebellion, and the emperor fled to Shimen.

sentences.zh: 緯從駕至莎城，疾漸危篤，先還京城。

translations.literal: Wei followed the carriage to Shacheng; his illness grew critical and he returned first to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei followed the carriage to Shacheng. His illness grew critical and he returned first to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，卒於光德里第，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he died at his mansion in Guangde Lane and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he died at his mansion in Guangde Lane and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 緯家尚節義，挺然不屈。

translations.literal: Wei's family valued integrity and stood upright without bending.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's family valued integrity and stood upright without bending.

sentences.zh: 雖權勢燻灼，未嘗假以恩禮。

translations.literal: Though power and influence blazed, they never sought favor through grace.
translations.idiomatic: Though power and influence blazed, they never sought favor through grace.

sentences.zh: 大順初，天武都頭李順節恃恩頗橫，不期年領浙西節度使，俄加平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Datong reign, Tianwu command head Li Shunjie relied on favor and was quite overbearing; within a year he held the Zhexi command and soon was made co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Datong era, Tianwu command head Li Shunjie relied on favor and was quite overbearing. Within a year he held the Zhexi command and soon was made co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 謝日，臺吏申中書，稱天武相公衙謝，準例班見百僚。

translations.literal: On the day of thanksgiving the censorial clerks reported to the Secretariat that the Tianwu chancellor's office gave thanks and, by precedent, would take rank before the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of thanksgiving the censorial clerks reported to the Secretariat that the Tianwu chancellor's office gave thanks and, by precedent, would take rank before the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 緯判曰：「不用立班。」

translations.literal: Wei ruled: 'No need to form ranks.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruled, "No need to form ranks."

sentences.zh: 順節麤暴小人，不閑朝法，盛飾趨中書，既見無班，心甚怏怏。

translations.literal: Shunjie was a coarse and violent petty man ignorant of court law; he dressed splendidly and hurried to the Secretariat. Seeing no ranks, he was deeply displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Shunjie was a coarse and violent petty man ignorant of court law. He dressed splendidly and hurried to the Secretariat. Seeing no ranks, he was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 他日因會，順節微言之。

translations.literal: Another day at a gathering Shunjie lightly mentioned it.
translations.idiomatic: Another day at a gathering Shunjie lightly mentioned it.

sentences.zh: 緯曰：「必知公慊也。

translations.literal: Wei said: 'You must know you are discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "You must know you are discontent.

sentences.zh: 夫百辟卿士，天子庭臣也，比來班見宰相，以輔臣居班列之首，奉長之義也。

translations.literal: The hundred ministers and grandees are courtiers of the Son of Heaven. Lately in taking rank before the chancellor, the assisting minister stood first in the ranks—the meaning of honoring elders.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred ministers and grandees are courtiers of the Son of Heaven. Lately in taking rank before the chancellor, the assisting minister stood first in the ranks—the meaning of honoring elders.

sentences.zh: 公握天武健兒，而於政事廳受百僚班見，意自安乎？

translations.literal: You hold Tianwu stalwarts yet receive the hundred officials' ranks in the hall of government—are you at ease in your mind?
translations.idiomatic: You hold Tianwu stalwarts yet receive the hundred officials' ranks in the hall of government—are you at ease in your mind?

sentences.zh: 必若須此儀，俟去『都頭』二字可也。」

translations.literal: If you truly need this ceremony, wait until the two characters 'command head' are removed.'
translations.idiomatic: If you truly need this ceremony, wait until the two characters 'command head' are removed."

sentences.zh: 順節不敢復言。

translations.literal: Shunjie dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: Shunjie dared speak no more.

sentences.zh: 其秉禮不回，多此類也。

translations.literal: His holding to ritual without yielding was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His holding to ritual without yielding was mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 孔氏自元和後，昆仲貴盛，至正卿、方鎮者六七人，未有爲宰輔者，至緯始在鼎司。

translations.literal: After the Yuanhe reign the Kong brothers were illustrious; six or seven reached regular ministers and regional commands, but none had been chancellor until Wei stood in the tripod office.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuanhe reign the Kong brothers were illustrious. Six or seven reached regular ministers and regional commands, but none had been chancellor until Wei stood in the tripod office.

sentences.zh: 子崇弼，亦登進士第，仕至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Chongbi also passed the jinshi and served to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongbi also passed the jinshi and served to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 韋昭度，字正紀，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaodu, style name Zhengji, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu, whose courtesy name was Zhengji, came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖縃，父逢。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Xu; his father Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Xu; his father Feng.

sentences.zh: 昭度，咸通八年進士擢第。

translations.literal: Zhaodu passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu passed the jinshi in the eighth year of Xiantong.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，累遷尚書郎、知制誥，正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu reign he was repeatedly promoted to Director of a Bureau and drafter of edicts, and formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era he was repeatedly promoted to Director of a Bureau and drafter of edicts, and formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗幸蜀，拜戸部侍郎，

translations.literal: Following Emperor Xizong to Shu, he was made vice minister of revenue
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Xizong to Shu, he was made vice minister of revenue

sentences.zh: 權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: and acting director of the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: and acting director of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年，以本官同平章事，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year, with his existing office he became co-chancellor and concurrently Minister of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, with his existing office he became co-chancellor and concurrently Minister of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，閬州刺史王建攻陳敬瑄於成都，隔絕貢奉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Lang Prefecture's Wang Jian attacked Chen Jingxuan at Chengdu and cut off tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Lang Prefecture's Wang Jian attacked Chen Jingxuan at Chengdu and cut off tribute.

sentences.zh: 乃以昭度檢校司空、同平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度招撫宣慰等使。

translations.literal: Zhaodu was made acting Minister of Works, co-chancellor, Governor of Chengdu, and military governor and pacification commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu was made acting Minister of Works, co-chancellor, Governor of Chengdu, and military governor and pacification commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 昭度赴鎮，敬瑄不受代。

translations.literal: Zhaodu went to his command; Jingxuan would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu went to his command; Jingxuan would not yield.

sentences.zh: 詔東川顧彥朗與王建合勢討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dongchuan's Gu Yanlang to join forces with Wang Jian to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Dongchuan's Gu Yanlang to join forces with Wang Jian to attack him.

sentences.zh: 昭度爲行營招討。

translations.literal: Zhaodu served as campaign pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu served as campaign pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒歲，止拔漢州。

translations.literal: By year's end they had taken only Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By year's end they had taken only Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王建謂昭度曰：「相公勞師弊眾，遠事蠻夷。

translations.literal: Wang Jian said to Zhaodu: 'Chancellor, you weary the army and exhaust the people in distant dealings with barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian said to Zhaodu, "Chancellor, you weary the army and exhaust the people in distant dealings with barbarians.

sentences.zh: 訪聞京洛以東，群侯相噬，禍難未已。

translations.literal: I hear that east of the capital the feudal lords devour one another and calamity has not ended.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that east of the capital the feudal lords devour one another and calamity has not ended.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不治，腹心之疾也。

translations.literal: The court does not govern—the disease is in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The court does not govern—the disease is in the heart.

sentences.zh: 相公宜亟還京師，咨謀匡合，平定兩河，國家之利也。

translations.literal: Chancellor, you should hurry back to the capital, consult and unite, and pacify the two He regions—this is the state's gain.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor, you should hurry back to the capital, consult and unite, and pacify the two He regions—this is the state's gain.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄小醜，以日月制之，擒之必矣！

translations.literal: Jingxuan is a petty villain; given time he can be taken and captured without fail!
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan is a petty villain. Given time he can be taken and captured without fail!

sentences.zh: 此事責建可辦。」

translations.literal: This matter can be entrusted to Jian.'
translations.idiomatic: This matter can be entrusted to Jian."

sentences.zh: 昭度然之，奏請還都。

translations.literal: Zhaodu agreed and memorialized to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu agreed and memorialized to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 昭度未及京師，建以重兵守劍門，急攻成都下之。

translations.literal: Before Zhaodu reached the capital, Jian held Jianmen with a heavy army and urgently attacked and took Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhaodu reached the capital, Jian held Jianmen with a heavy army and urgently attacked and took Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 殺敬瑄，自稱留後。

translations.literal: He killed Jingxuan and styled himself acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Jingxuan and styled himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 昭度還，以檢校司空充東都留守。

translations.literal: Zhaodu returned and was made acting Minister of Works and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu returned and was made acting Minister of Works and Defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 召還，爲右僕射。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 先是，邠州王行瑜求爲尚書令，昭度奏議云：「國朝已來，功如郭子儀，未省曾兼此官。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Bin Prefecture's Wang Xingyu had asked to be Director of the Department of State; Zhaodu memorialized: 'Since our dynasty began, even one with merit like Guo Ziyi has never held this office.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bin Prefecture's Wang Xingyu had asked to be Director of the Department of State. Zhaodu memorialized, "Since our dynasty began, even one with merit like Guo Ziyi has never held this office."

sentences.zh: 乃賜號「尚父」。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given the title 'Sagely Father.'
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was given the title 'Sagely Father.'

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯宗人鋌，曾爲行瑜從事，朝廷每降制敕，不便於昭緯者，即令鋌訴於行瑜，俾上章論列。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei's clansman Ting had once been Xingyu's aide; whenever court edicts were inconvenient for Zhaowei, he had Ting complain to Xingyu and induce him to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei's clansman Ting had once been Xingyu's aide. Whenever court edicts were inconvenient for Zhaowei, he had Ting complain to Xingyu and induce him to submit memorials.

sentences.zh: 朝旨小有依違，即表章不遜。

translations.literal: Whenever court intent wavered slightly, he submitted impertinent memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court intent wavered slightly, he submitted impertinent memorials.

sentences.zh: 至是李谿入拜。

translations.literal: At this time Li Xi entered appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Xi entered appointment.

sentences.zh: 昭緯謂鋌曰：「前時尚父之命已行，而昭度沮之，今又引谿同列。

translations.literal: Zhaowei said to Ting: 'Before, the Sagely Father's appointment had already been issued, yet Zhaodu obstructed it. Now he again brings Xi into the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowei said to Ting, "Before, the Sagely Father's appointment had already been issued, yet Zhaodu obstructed it. Now he again brings Xi into the same rank.

sentences.zh: 此人姦纎，惑上視聽，宗社不寧。

translations.literal: This man is treacherous and subtle, confusing what the sovereign sees and hears—the ancestral temple is not secure.
translations.idiomatic: This man is treacherous and subtle, confusing what the sovereign sees and hears—the ancestral temple is not secure.

sentences.zh: 恐復有杜太尉之事。」

translations.literal: I fear there will again be the affair of Grand Marshal Du.'
translations.idiomatic: I fear there will again be the affair of Grand Marshal Du."

sentences.zh: 行瑜與李茂貞上章言：「命相非其人，懼危宗社。」

translations.literal: Xingyu and Li Maozhen submitted memorials saying: 'The appointment of chancellors is not the right men—we fear danger to the ancestral temple.'
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu and Li Maozhen submitted memorials saying, "The appointment of chancellors is not the right men—we fear danger to the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 天子優詔曉諭，言谿有才。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven replied with a gracious edict explaining that Xi had talent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict explaining that Xi had talent.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，行瑜、茂貞、華州韓建以兵入覲，面奏昭度、李谿之姦邪，請加譴逐。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month Xingyu, Maozhen, and Hua's Han Jian entered audience with troops and memorialized face to face that Zhaodu and Li Xi were wicked; they asked that punishment and exile be added.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the fifth month Xingyu, Maozhen, and Hua's Han Jian entered audience with troops and memorialized face to face that Zhaodu and Li Xi were wicked. They asked that punishment and exile be added.

sentences.zh: 制敕未行，三鎮兵害昭度於都亭驛。

translations.literal: Before the edict was issued, the three commands' troops killed Zhaodu at Duting Station.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict was issued, the three commands' troops killed Zhaodu at Duting Station.

sentences.zh: 及行瑜誅，降制復其官爵，令其家收葬。

translations.literal: When Xingyu was executed, an edict restored his offices and ordered his family to collect the body for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingyu was executed, an edict restored his offices and ordered his family to collect the body for burial.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯，清河人也。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei was a native of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖庇，滑州酸棗縣尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bi was magistrate of Suanzao County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bi was magistrate of Suanzao County in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父巘，鄂州觀察使。

translations.literal: His father Yan was governor of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was governor of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昭緯進士及第。

translations.literal: Zhaowei passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowei passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 昭宗朝，歷中書舍人、翰林學士、戸部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In Zhaozong's reign he successively served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Hanlin academician, vice minister of revenue, and co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhaozong's reign he successively served as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Hanlin academician, vice minister of revenue, and co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 性姦纎，忌前達。

translations.literal: By nature he was treacherous and subtle and jealous of his predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was treacherous and subtle and jealous of his predecessors.

sentences.zh: 內結中人，外連籓閫。

translations.literal: Within he joined with inner officials; outside he connected with regional gates.
translations.idiomatic: Within he joined with inner officials; outside he connected with regional gates.

sentences.zh: 屬朝廷微弱，每托援以淩人主。

translations.literal: As the court grew weak, he always relied on support to bully the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: As the court grew weak, he always relied on support to bully the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 昭宗明察，心不能堪。

translations.literal: Zhaozong was perceptive and could not bear it in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong was perceptive and could not bear it in his heart.

sentences.zh: 以誘召三鎮將兵詣闕，賊殺宰輔內臣，帝深切齒。

translations.literal: By inducing the three commands to bring troops to court, bandits killed chancellors and inner officials; the emperor deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: By inducing the three commands to bring troops to court, bandits killed chancellors and inner officials. The emperor deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 會太原之師誅行瑜，罷相，授右僕射。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan's army executed Xingyu, Zhaowei was removed as chancellor and made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan's army executed Xingyu, Zhaowei was removed as chancellor and made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 後又以托附汴州，再貶梧州司馬。

translations.literal: Later, for relying on Bian Prefecture, he was again demoted to assistant prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for relying on Bian Prefecture, he was again demoted to assistant prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋降制曰：

translations.literal: Soon an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict said:

sentences.zh: 又快其私忿，輒恣陰謀。

translations.literal: Again indulging private resentment, you freely plotted in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Again indulging private resentment, you freely plotted in secret.

sentences.zh: 托崔鋌之險巇，連行瑜之計畫，遂致稱兵向闕，怙眾脅君。

translations.literal: Relying on Cui Ting's treachery, you linked with Xingyu's plans, and thus troops were called to the capital, relying on numbers to coerce the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on Cui Ting's treachery, you linked with Xingyu's plans, and thus troops were called to the capital, relying on numbers to coerce the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 故宰臣韋昭度、李谿並以無辜見害，幾危宗社，顯辱君親。

translations.literal: Former chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi were both killed without guilt, nearly endangering the ancestral temple and openly shaming ruler and parent.
translations.idiomatic: Former chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi were both killed without guilt, nearly endangering the ancestral temple and openly shaming ruler and parent.

sentences.zh: 爾罪二也。

translations.literal: This is your second crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is your second crime.

sentences.zh: 及行瑜敗滅，京國甫安，而乃自懼欺誣，別謀托附。

translations.literal: When Xingyu was defeated and destroyed and the capital was just pacified, you then feared exposure of your deceit and plotted other attachments.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingyu was defeated and destroyed and the capital was just pacified, you then feared exposure of your deceit and plotted other attachments.

sentences.zh: 又於籓閫，潛請薦論，不唯茍免罪愆，兼亦再希任用。

translations.literal: Again at regional gates you secretly asked for recommendation and discussion—not only to escape guilt, but also again to hope for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Again at regional gates you secretly asked for recommendation and discussion—not only to escape guilt, but also again to hope for appointment.

sentences.zh: 貪榮冒寵，僭濫無厭，敗俗傷風，賢愚共鄙。

translations.literal: Greedy for glory and courting favor, presumptuous and excessive without end—you corrupted custom and wounded integrity; wise and foolish alike despised you.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for glory and courting favor, presumptuous and excessive without end—you corrupted custom and wounded integrity. Wise and foolish alike despised you.

sentences.zh: 爾罪三也。

translations.literal: This is your third crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is your third crime.

sentences.zh: 又將厚賂，欲結諸王，輕侮我憲章，玷瀆我骨肉。

translations.literal: Again with heavy bribes you wished to bind the princes, lightly insulting our statutes and defiling our flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: Again with heavy bribes you wished to bind the princes, lightly insulting our statutes and defiling our flesh and blood.

sentences.zh: 貨財之數，文字具存。

translations.literal: The amount of goods and the written records still exist.
translations.idiomatic: The amount of goods and the written records still exist.

sentences.zh: 賴諸王作朕腹心，嫉其蠹害，盡將昭緯情款，兼其親吏姓名，直具奏聞，拒其求托。

translations.literal: Fortunately the princes serve as our heart and belly, hating your corruption; they fully reported Zhaowei's circumstances and the names of his intimate clerks, submitted directly, and refused his requests.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the princes serve as our heart and belly, hating your corruption. They fully reported Zhaowei's circumstances and the names of his intimate clerks, submitted directly, and refused his requests.

sentences.zh: 昭緯曾居宰輔，久歷清崇，但欲逞其回邪，都不顧其事體。

translations.literal: Zhaowei once stood as chancellor and long held lofty office, yet only wished to display his perversity and wholly disregarded what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowei once stood as chancellor and long held lofty office, yet only wished to display his perversity and wholly disregarded what was fitting.

sentences.zh: 觀其識見，實駭聽聞。

translations.literal: Viewing his insight, it truly shocks the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Viewing his insight, it truly shocks the ear.

sentences.zh: 爾罪四也。

translations.literal: This is your fourth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is your fourth crime.

sentences.zh: 自姦邪既露，情狀難容。

translations.literal: Since treachery was exposed and the facts could not be borne,
translations.idiomatic: Since treachery was exposed and the facts could not be borne,

sentences.zh: 尚示寬刑，未行嚴憲，投於荒裔，冀其自新。

translations.literal: lenient punishment was still shown and severe law was not applied; you were sent to the wild border in hope you would reform.
translations.idiomatic: lenient punishment was still shown and severe law was not applied. You were sent to the wild border in hope you would reform.

sentences.zh: 而不能退省過尤，恭承制命，速赴貶所，用守常規。

translations.literal: Yet you could not withdraw and reflect on your faults, respectfully accept the edict, and hurry to the place of demotion to keep ordinary rules.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you could not withdraw and reflect on your faults, respectfully accept the edict, and hurry to the place of demotion to keep ordinary rules.

sentences.zh: 而猶自務宴安，尋聞所在留駐；

translations.literal: Instead you still sought ease and pleasure, and soon were heard to linger where you were;
translations.idiomatic: Instead you still sought ease and pleasure, and soon were heard to linger where you were.

sentences.zh: 攪擾籓鎮，侮慢朝章。

translations.literal: disturbing regional commands and insulting court statutes.
translations.idiomatic: disturbing regional commands and insulting court statutes.

sentences.zh: 曾無稟畏之心，可驗苞藏之計。

translations.literal: There was no heart of fear and respect—your hidden designs can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: There was no heart of fear and respect—your hidden designs can be verified.

sentences.zh: 罔知愆咎，唯謗朝廷。

translations.literal: You knew no guilt and only slandered the court.
