translations.idiomatic: You knew no guilt and only slandered the court.

sentences.zh: 爾罪五也。

translations.literal: This is your fifth crime.
translations.idiomatic: This is your fifth crime.

sentences.zh: 朕以恩澤者，帝王之雨露，弄法者，邦國之雷霆；

translations.literal: We regard grace as the rain and dew of emperors; those who toy with law are the thunder of the state.
translations.idiomatic: We regard grace as the rain and dew of emperors. Those who toy with law are the thunder of the state.

sentences.zh: 無雨露則庶物不榮，無雷霆則萬邦不肅。

translations.literal: Without rain and dew the multitude does not flourish; without thunder the myriad states are not awed.
translations.idiomatic: Without rain and dew the multitude does not flourish. Without thunder the myriad states are not awed.

sentences.zh: 朕體天道以化育，遵王度以澄清，罪既昭彰，理難含垢。

translations.literal: We embody Heaven's way in nurturing and follow royal measure in clarifying; guilt is manifest and principle cannot harbor filth.
translations.idiomatic: We embody Heaven's way in nurturing and follow royal measure in clarifying. Guilt is manifest and principle cannot harbor filth.

sentences.zh: 凡百多士，宜體予懷。

translations.literal: All you many officers should embody our intent.
translations.idiomatic: All you many officers should embody our intent.

sentences.zh: 宜所在賜自盡。

translations.literal: Where you are, you should be ordered to take your own life.
translations.idiomatic: Where you are, you should be ordered to take your own life.

sentences.zh: 時昭緯行次至荊南，中使至，斬之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhaowei was at Jingnan when the inner envoy arrived and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhaowei was at Jingnan when the inner envoy arrived and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 兄昭符，仕至禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhaofu served to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhaofu served to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 昭願，太子少保。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan was Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan was Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 昭矩，給事中。

translations.literal: Zhaoju was Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoju was Attendant.

sentences.zh: 昭遠，考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan was vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan was vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 張濬，字禹川，河間人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, style name Yuchuan, was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, whose courtesy name was Yuchuan, came from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 祖仲素，位至中書舍人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhongsu served to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhongsu served to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父鐐，官卑，家寓州。

translations.literal: His father Liao held a low office; the family dwelt in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liao held a low office; the family dwelt in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 濬倜儻不羈，涉獵文史，好大言，爲士友之所擯棄。

translations.literal: Jun was unconventional and unrestrained, widely read in literature and history, fond of grand talk, and was cast aside by scholar friends.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was unconventional and unrestrained, widely read in literature and history, fond of grand talk, and was cast aside by scholar friends.

sentences.zh: 初從鄉賦隨計，咸薄其爲人。

translations.literal: At first when he followed the local examination to the capital, all in Xian looked down on his character.
translations.idiomatic: At first when he followed the local examination to the capital, all in Xian looked down on his character.

sentences.zh: 濬憤憤不得志，乃田衣野服，隱於金鳳山，學鬼谷縱橫之術，欲以捭闔取貴仕。

translations.literal: Jun, indignant and unfulfilled, then wore field clothes and rustic garb and hid on Golden Phoenix Mountain, studying Guiguzi's alliance-and-division arts, wishing to rise to high office through maneuver.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, indignant and unfulfilled, then wore field clothes and rustic garb and hid on Golden Phoenix Mountain, studying Guiguzi's alliance-and-division arts, wishing to rise to high office through maneuver.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，樞密使楊復恭因使遇之，自處士薦爲太常博士，累轉度支員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu reign Palace Commissioner Yang Fugong, meeting him on a mission, recommended the recluse as Doctor of the Grand Temple and repeatedly promoted him to vice director of the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era Palace Commissioner Yang Fugong, meeting him on a mission, recommended the recluse as Doctor of the Grand Temple and repeatedly promoted him to vice director of the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 黃巢將逼關輔，濬托疾請告，侍其母，挈族避亂商州。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao was about to press the capital region, Jun pleaded illness and asked leave to attend his mother, taking his clan to flee the chaos in Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao was about to press the capital region, Jun pleaded illness and asked leave to attend his mother, taking his clan to flee the chaos in Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊犯京師，僖宗出幸，途無供頓，衛軍不得食。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked the capital, Emperor Xizong fled; along the road there were no supplies and the guard army had no food.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits attacked the capital, Emperor Xizong fled. Along the road there were no supplies and the guard army had no food.

sentences.zh: 漢陰令李康獻糗餌數百騾綱，軍士始得食。

translations.literal: Hanyin magistrate Li Kang presented several hundred strings of mules with grain cakes, and the soldiers finally had food.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyin magistrate Li Kang presented several hundred strings of mules with grain cakes, and the soldiers finally had food.

sentences.zh: 僖宗召康問曰：「卿爲縣令，安操心及此？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong summoned Kang and asked: 'As magistrate, how did you take this to heart?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong summoned Kang and asked, "As magistrate, how did you take this to heart?"

sentences.zh: 康對曰：「臣爲塵吏，敢有此進獻？

translations.literal: Kang replied: 'I am a lowly clerk—how dare I make such presentation?
translations.idiomatic: Kang replied, "I am a lowly clerk—how dare I make such presentation?

sentences.zh: 張濬員外教臣也。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Zhang Jun outside the regular ranks taught me.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhang Jun outside the regular ranks taught me."

sentences.zh: 帝異之，急召至行在，拜兵部郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor was struck and urgently summoned Jun to the temporary court, appointing him Director of the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck and urgently summoned Jun to the temporary court, appointing him Director of the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Remonstrating Official.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Remonstrating Official.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，宰相王鐸至滑臺，兼充天下行營都統。

translations.literal: That winter Chancellor Wang Duo reached Hua Terrace and concurrently served as overall commander of the campaign armies of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chancellor Wang Duo reached Hua Terrace and concurrently served as overall commander of the campaign armies of the realm.

sentences.zh: 方征兵諸侯，奏用濬爲都統判官。

translations.literal: As he was recruiting troops from the feudal lords, he memorialized Jun as adjutant to the overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: As he was recruiting troops from the feudal lords, he memorialized Jun as adjutant to the overall commander.

sentences.zh: 時王敬武初破弘霸郎，軍威大振，累詔征平盧兵，敬武獨不赴援。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jingwu had just defeated Hong Ba Lang; his army's prestige was greatly raised. Repeated edicts summoned Pinglu troops, but Jingwu alone did not come to aid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Jingwu had just defeated Hong Ba Lang. His army's prestige was greatly raised. Repeated edicts summoned Pinglu troops, but Jingwu alone did not come to aid.

sentences.zh: 鐸遣濬往說之，敬武已受偽命，復怙強不迎詔使。

translations.literal: Duo sent Jun to persuade him. Jingwu had already accepted a false appointment and again relied on his strength and did not welcome the edict envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Duo sent Jun to persuade him. Jingwu had already accepted a false appointment and again relied on his strength and did not welcome the edict envoy.

sentences.zh: 濬至，謁見，責之曰：「公爲天子守籓，王臣賫詔宣諭，而侮慢詔使。

translations.literal: When Jun arrived and had audience, he reproached him: 'You guard a circuit for the Son of Heaven. A royal minister bears the edict to proclaim—and you insult the edict envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun arrived and had audience, he reproached him, "You guard a circuit for the Son of Heaven. A royal minister bears the edict to proclaim—and you insult the edict envoy.

sentences.zh: 既未識君臣禮分，復何顏以御軍民哉？」

translations.literal: Not knowing the ritual between ruler and subject, what face have you to command army and people?'
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing the ritual between ruler and subject, what face have you to command army and people?"

sentences.zh: 敬武愕然謝咎。

translations.literal: Jingwu was startled and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu was startled and apologized.

sentences.zh: 既宣詔，軍士按兵默然，濬並召將佐集於鞠場面諭之曰：「人生效忠仗義，所冀粗分順逆，懸知利害。

translations.literal: After proclaiming the edict, the soldiers held their arms in silence. Jun also summoned generals and staff to the drill ground and addressed them face to face: 'In life one serves loyalty and righteousness, hoping only to distinguish obedience from rebellion and know gain from harm.
translations.idiomatic: After proclaiming the edict, the soldiers held their arms in silence. Jun also summoned generals and staff to the drill ground and addressed them face to face, "In life one serves loyalty and righteousness, hoping only to distinguish obedience from rebellion and know gain from harm.

sentences.zh: 黃巢前日販鹽虜耳，公等舍累葉天子而臣販鹽白丁，何利害之可論耶？

translations.literal: Huang Chao was formerly a salt peddler—yet you abandon generations of the Son of Heaven to serve a salt-peddling commoner. What gain or harm can be discussed?
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao was formerly a salt peddler—yet you abandon generations of the Son of Heaven to serve a salt-peddling commoner. What gain or harm can be discussed?

sentences.zh: 今諸侯勤王，天下響應，公等獨據一州，坐觀成敗。

translations.literal: Now the feudal lords aid the throne and the realm responds; you alone hold one prefecture and sit watching success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Now the feudal lords aid the throne and the realm responds. You alone hold one prefecture and sit watching success or failure.

sentences.zh: 賊平之後，去就何安？

translations.literal: After the bandits are pacified, where will you stand?
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits are pacified, where will you stand?

sentences.zh: 若能此際排難解紛，陳師鞠旅，共誅寇盜，迎奉鑾輿，則富貴功名，指掌可取。

translations.literal: If at this moment you resolve difficulty and untie strife, array troops and drill the army, together exterminate the robbers and welcome the imperial carriage, then wealth, glory, and merit are within your grasp.
translations.idiomatic: If at this moment you resolve difficulty and untie strife, array troops and drill the army, together exterminate the robbers and welcome the imperial carriage, then wealth, glory, and merit are within your grasp.

sentences.zh: 吾惜公輩舍安而即危也！」

translations.literal: I pity you gentlemen for leaving safety and rushing into peril!'
translations.idiomatic: I pity you gentlemen for leaving safety and rushing into peril!"

sentences.zh: 諸將改容引過，謂敬武曰：「諫議之言是也。」

translations.literal: The generals changed expression and admitted fault, saying to Jingwu: 'The Remonstrating Official's words are right.'
translations.idiomatic: The generals changed expression and admitted fault, saying to Jingwu, "The Remonstrating Official's words are right."

sentences.zh: 即時出軍，從濬入援京師。

translations.literal: At once they marched out and followed Jun to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At once they marched out and followed Jun to aid the capital.

sentences.zh: 賊平，累遷戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Jun was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were pacified, Jun was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 僖宗再幸山南，拜平章事、判度支。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong again proceeded to Shannan, Jun was made co-chancellor and put in charge of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong again proceeded to Shannan, Jun was made co-chancellor and put in charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 濬初發跡，依楊復恭。

translations.literal: When Jun first rose, he relied on Yang Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun first rose, he relied on Yang Fugong.

sentences.zh: 及復恭失勢，乃依田令孜，以至重位，而反薄復恭。

translations.literal: When Fugong lost power he relied on Tian Lingzi, reaching the highest post, yet in turn looked down on Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: When Fugong lost power he relied on Tian Lingzi, reaching the highest post, yet in turn looked down on Fugong.

sentences.zh: 及再幸山南，復恭代令孜爲中尉，罷濬知政事。

translations.literal: When the emperor again proceeded to Shannan, Fugong replaced Lingzi as commander and removed Jun from handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor again proceeded to Shannan, Fugong replaced Lingzi as commander and removed Jun from handling state affairs.

sentences.zh: 昭宗初在籓邸，深嫉宦官，復恭有援立大勛，恃恩任事，上心不平之。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong was first in the princely residence he deeply hated eunuchs; Fugong had great merit in supporting enthronement and relied on favor to handle affairs—the sovereign's heart was unequal.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong was first in the princely residence he deeply hated eunuchs. Fugong had great merit in supporting enthronement and relied on favor to handle affairs—the sovereign's heart was unequal.

sentences.zh: 當時趨向者，多言濬有方略，能畫大計，復用爲宰相、判度支。

translations.literal: Those who sought favor then often said Jun had strategy and could plan great affairs; he was again used as chancellor and put in charge of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought favor then often said Jun had strategy and could plan great affairs. He was again used as chancellor and put in charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問濬，致理何事最急？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Jun what matter in ordering the state was most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Jun what matter in ordering the state was most urgent.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「莫若強兵。

translations.literal: He replied: 'Nothing like strengthening the army.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Nothing like strengthening the army.

sentences.zh: 兵強而天下服。」

translations.literal: When the army is strong the realm submits.'
translations.idiomatic: When the army is strong the realm submits."

sentences.zh: 上由是專務搜補兵甲，欲以武功勝天下。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore devoted himself to gathering weapons and armor, wishing to overcome the realm by military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore devoted himself to gathering weapons and armor, wishing to overcome the realm by military achievement.

sentences.zh: 後延英論前代爲治得失，濬曰：「不必遠征漢、晉之弊。

translations.literal: Later in Yanying they discussed the gains and losses of rule in former ages; Jun said: 'There is no need to go far and cite the flaws of Han and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Later in Yanying they discussed the gains and losses of rule in former ages. Jun said, "There is no need to go far and cite the flaws of Han and Jin.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見陛下春秋鼎盛，英睿如此，內外逼於強臣。

translations.literal: I privately see Your Majesty in the prime of youth, so bright and keen—yet inside and outside you are pressed by powerful ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I privately see Your Majesty in the prime of youth, so bright and keen—yet inside and outside you are pressed by powerful ministers.

sentences.zh: 臣每思之，實痛心而泣血也。」

translations.literal: Whenever I think of it, I truly ache in heart and weep blood.'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of it, I truly ache in heart and weep blood."

sentences.zh: 會朱全忠誅秦宗權，安居受殺李克恭，以潞州降全忠。

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong executed Qin Zongquan, he peacefully received the killing of Li Kegong and with Lu Prefecture surrendered to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong executed Qin Zongquan, he peacefully received the killing of Li Kegong and with Lu Prefecture surrendered to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 幽州李匡威、雲州赫連鐸等奏請出軍討太原。

translations.literal: Youzhou's Li Kuangwei, Yun Prefecture's Helian Tuo, and others memorialized asking to march out against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou's Li Kuangwei, Yun Prefecture's Helian Tuo, and others memorialized asking to march out against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔四品以上官議，皆言：「國祚未安，不宜生事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials of the fourth rank and above to discuss; all said: 'The dynastic fortune is not yet secure; one should not stir trouble.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials of the fourth rank and above to discuss. All said, "The dynastic fortune is not yet secure; one should not stir trouble.

sentences.zh: 假如得太原，亦非國家所有。」

translations.literal: Even if Taiyuan were taken, it would not belong to the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Even if Taiyuan were taken, it would not belong to the state."

sentences.zh: 濬議曰：「先帝頻至播越，王室不寧。

translations.literal: Jun argued: 'The former emperor repeatedly wandered in exile and the royal house was not secure.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued, "The former emperor repeatedly wandered in exile and the royal house was not secure.

sentences.zh: 原其亂階，由克用、全忠之矛盾也。

translations.literal: Tracing the steps of disorder, it came from the conflict between Keyong and Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the steps of disorder, it came from the conflict between Keyong and Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 請因其奏，乘全忠立功，可斷兩雄之勢。」

translations.literal: Please take advantage of their memorial, while Quanzhong has merit, to cut the power of the two heroes.'
translations.idiomatic: Please take advantage of their memorial, while Quanzhong has merit, to cut the power of the two heroes."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「收復之功，克用第一。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'In merit of recovery Keyong was first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In merit of recovery Keyong was first.

sentences.zh: 今乘其危困而加兵，諸侯其謂我何？」

translations.literal: Now to add troops while he is in peril and distress—what will the feudal lords say of us?'
translations.idiomatic: Now to add troops while he is in peril and distress—what will the feudal lords say of us?"

sentences.zh: 濬懇論用兵之利害，蓋欲示外勢而擠復恭也。

translations.literal: Jun earnestly argued the gain and harm of using troops, essentially wishing to show external force and squeeze Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: Jun earnestly argued the gain and harm of using troops, essentially wishing to show external force and squeeze Fugong.

sentences.zh: 上旨未決。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's intent was undecided.

sentences.zh: 宰臣孔緯曰：「張濬所陳，萬代之利也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Kong Wei said: 'What Zhang Jun stated is benefit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Kong Wei said, "What Zhang Jun stated is benefit for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 陛下所惜，即日之利也。

translations.literal: What Your Majesty regrets is benefit of the day.
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty regrets is benefit of the day.

sentences.zh: 以臣所料，師渡河而賊必自破。

translations.literal: By my reckoning, once the army crosses the river the bandit will surely break by itself.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning, once the army crosses the river the bandit will surely break by itself.

sentences.zh: 昨計度軍中轉餉犒勞，一二年間，必無闕事，陛下斷意行之。」

translations.literal: Yesterday in calculating transport, rewards, and provisions for the army, within one or two years there will certainly be no lack. Your Majesty should resolve and act.'
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday in calculating transport, rewards, and provisions for the army, within one or two years there will certainly be no lack. Your Majesty should resolve and act."

sentences.zh: 既二相俱論，乃以濬爲河東行營兵馬都招討宣慰使，以京兆尹孫揆副之。

translations.literal: When both chancellors had argued, Jun was made overall pacification and comfort commissioner of the Hedong campaign armies, with Metropolitan Governor Sun Kui as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When both chancellors had argued, Jun was made overall pacification and comfort commissioner of the Hedong campaign armies, with Metropolitan Governor Sun Kui as deputy.

sentences.zh: 仍授揆昭義節度使，華州韓建爲供軍使，朱全忠爲太原西南面招討使，李匡威、赫連鐸爲太原東北面招討使。

translations.literal: Kui was also made military governor of Zhaoyi; Hua's Han Jian was supply commissioner; Zhu Quanzhong was southwest campaign commissioner against Taiyuan; Li Kuangwei and Helian Tuo were northeast campaign commissioners against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was also made military governor of Zhaoyi; Hua's Han Jian was supply commissioner; Zhu Quanzhong was southwest campaign commissioner against Taiyuan; Li Kuangwei and Helian Tuo were northeast campaign commissioners against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 全忠以汴軍三千爲濬牙隊。

translations.literal: Quanzhong gave three thousand Bian troops as Jun's guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong gave three thousand Bian troops as Jun's guard corps.

sentences.zh: 六月，濬率軍五十二都，兼邠寧、鄜、夏雜虜共五萬人騎，發自京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Jun led fifty-two commands of troops, together with Binning, Yan, and Xia mixed barbarians—altogether fifty thousand cavalry—and set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Jun led fifty-two commands of troops, together with Binning, Yan, and Xia mixed barbarians—altogether fifty thousand cavalry—and set out from the capital.

sentences.zh: 昭宗御安喜樓臨送，濬酒酣泣奏曰：「陛下動爲賊臣掣肘，臣所以誓死憤惋，爲陛下除其僭逼。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong faced Anxi Tower to send them off. Jun, tipsy with wine, wept and memorialized: 'Your Majesty's every move is checked by treacherous ministers. I therefore vow to die in indignation and remove their presumptuous coercion for Your Majesty.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong faced Anxi Tower to send them off. Jun, tipsy with wine, wept and memorialized, "Your Majesty's every move is checked by treacherous ministers. I therefore vow to die in indignation and remove their presumptuous coercion for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 楊復恭聞之不悅。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong heard it and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong heard it and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 中尉內使餞於長樂，復恭奉巵酒屬濬，濬辭曰：「聖人賜酒，已醉矣。」

translations.literal: The commanders of the palace armies and inner attendants gave a farewell feast at Changle; Fugong raised a cup of wine and offered it to Jun. Jun declined: 'The sage has given wine—I am already drunk.'
translations.idiomatic: The commanders of the palace armies and inner attendants gave a farewell feast at Changle. Fugong raised a cup of wine and offered it to Jun. Jun declined, "The sage has given wine—I am already drunk."

sentences.zh: 復恭戲曰：「相公握禁兵，擁大蒐，獨當一面，不領復恭意作面子耶！」

translations.literal: Fugong jested: 'Chancellor, you hold the forbidden armies and lead a great hunt, alone facing one direction—will you not heed Fugong's intent and show face?'
translations.idiomatic: Fugong jested, "Chancellor, you hold the forbidden armies and lead a great hunt, alone facing one direction—will you not heed Fugong's intent and show face?"

sentences.zh: 濬笑曰：「賊平之後，方見面子。」

translations.literal: Jun laughed: 'After the bandits are pacified, then you will see face.'
translations.idiomatic: Jun laughed, "After the bandits are pacified, then you will see face."

sentences.zh: 復恭銜之。

translations.literal: Fugong bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 時汴、華、邠、岐之師渡河，會濬於晉州。

translations.literal: At that time the Bian, Hua, Bin, and Qi armies crossed the river and met Jun at Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Bian, Hua, Bin, and Qi armies crossed the river and met Jun at Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 汴將朱崇節權知潞州事，太原將李存孝攻之。

translations.literal: Bian general Zhu Chongjie was acting governor of Lu Prefecture; Taiyuan general Li Cunxiao attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Bian general Zhu Chongjie was acting governor of Lu Prefecture. Taiyuan general Li Cunxiao attacked him.

sentences.zh: 濬慮賊平汴人據昭義，乃令孫揆分兵赴鎮，中使韓歸範送旌節至軍。

translations.literal: Jun feared that after the bandits were pacified Bian men would hold Zhaoyi; he therefore ordered Sun Kui to divide troops and go to the command, and inner envoy Han Guifan delivered the banner and tally to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jun feared that after the bandits were pacified Bian men would hold Zhaoyi. He therefore ordered Sun Kui to divide troops and go to the command, and inner envoy Han Guifan delivered the banner and tally to the army.

sentences.zh: 八月，揆與歸範赴潞州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Kui and Guifan went to Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Kui and Guifan went to Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至潞，並爲存孝擒送太原。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Lu, both were seized by Cunxiao and sent to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Lu, both were seized by Cunxiao and sent to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 九月，汴將葛從周棄潞州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Bian general Ge Congzhou abandoned Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Bian general Ge Congzhou abandoned Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月，濬軍至陰地，邠、岐、華三鎮之師營平陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Jun's army reached Yindi; the Bin, Qi, and Hua armies camped at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Jun's army reached Yindi. The Bin, Qi, and Hua armies camped at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 李存孝擊之，一戰而敗，委兵仗潰散。

translations.literal: Li Cunxiao attacked them; in one battle they were defeated and cast away weapons in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxiao attacked them. In one battle they were defeated and cast away weapons in rout.

sentences.zh: 進攻晉州。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to attack Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數日，中夜濬斂眾遁走。

translations.literal: After several days, in the middle of the night Jun gathered his forces and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, in the middle of the night Jun gathered his forces and fled.

sentences.zh: 比曙，喪師殆半。

translations.literal: By dawn nearly half the army was lost.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn nearly half the army was lost.

sentences.zh: 存孝進收晉、絳、慈、隰等州。

translations.literal: Cunxiao advanced and recovered Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao advanced and recovered Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 濬狼狽由含山逾王屋，出河清，拆屋木縛筏濟河，部下離散將盡。

translations.literal: Jun in disarray crossed Hanshan, passed Wangwu, emerged at Heqing, tore house timbers to bind rafts and cross the river; his subordinates scattered nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Jun in disarray crossed Hanshan, passed Wangwu, emerged at Heqing, tore house timbers to bind rafts and cross the river. His subordinates scattered nearly to the last.

sentences.zh: 李克用上章論訴曰：

translations.literal: Li Keyong submitted a memorial of protest:
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong submitted a memorial of protest:

sentences.zh: 況臣父子三代，受恩四朝，破徐方，救荊楚，收鳳闕，碎梟巢，致陛下今日冠通天之冠，佩白玉之璽。

translations.literal: Moreover my father and son for three generations received grace through four reigns, broke Xu region, rescued Jing-Chu, recovered the Phoenix Gate, shattered the owl nest—bringing Your Majesty today to wear the heaven-reaching cap and carry the white jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my father and son for three generations received grace through four reigns, broke Xu region, rescued Jing-Chu, recovered the Phoenix Gate, shattered the owl nest—bringing Your Majesty today to wear the heaven-reaching cap and carry the white jade seal.

sentences.zh: 臣之屬籍，懿皇所賜；

translations.literal: My clan register was bestowed by Emperor Yizong;
translations.idiomatic: My clan register was bestowed by Emperor Yizong.

sentences.zh: 臣之師律，先帝所命。

translations.literal: my military command was appointed by the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: My military command was appointed by the former emperor.

sentences.zh: 臣無逆節，濬討何名？

translations.literal: I have no rebellious conduct—under what name does Jun attack?
translations.idiomatic: I have no rebellious conduct—under what name does Jun attack?

sentences.zh: 陛下若厭逐功臣，欲用文吏，自可遷臣封邑，以侯就第。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty tires of expelling meritorious ministers and wishes to use civil officials, you may simply transfer my fief and let me retire as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty tires of expelling meritorious ministers and wishes to use civil officials, you may simply transfer my fief and let me retire as marquis.

sentences.zh: 奈何加諸其罪，孰肯無詞？

translations.literal: Why add crimes—who would be without words?
translations.idiomatic: Why add crimes—who would be without words?

sentences.zh: 若以臣雲中之伐，獲罪於時，則拓拔思恭取鄜、延，朱全忠侵徐、鄆，陛下何不討之？

translations.literal: If because of my Yunzhong campaign I was guilty at the time, then why not attack Tuoba Sichong for taking Yan and Yan, or Zhu Quanzhong for invading Xu and Yun?
translations.idiomatic: If because of my Yunzhong campaign I was guilty at the time, then why not attack Tuoba Sichong for taking Yan and Yan, or Zhu Quanzhong for invading Xu and Yun?

sentences.zh: 假令李孝德不忠於主，伐之爲是，則朱瑄、時溥有何罪耶？

translations.literal: Suppose Li Xiaode were disloyal to his lord and attacking him were right—what crime have Zhu Xuan and Shi Pu?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose Li Xiaode were disloyal to his lord and attacking him were right—what crime have Zhu Xuan and Shi Pu?

sentences.zh: 此乃同坐而異名，賞彼而誅此，使天下籓服，強者扼腕，弱者自動，流言竊議，爲臣怨嗟，固非中興之術也。

translations.literal: This is the same seat with different names, rewarding them while executing me—making the realm's commands submit while the strong clench their wrists and the weak tremble, with slander and secret talk, subjects groaning in resentment. This is truly not the method of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: This is the same seat with different names, rewarding them while executing me—making the realm's commands submit while the strong clench their wrists and the weak tremble, with slander and secret talk and subjects groaning in resentment. This is truly not the method of restoration.

sentences.zh: 且陛下阽危之秋，則獎臣爲韓、彭、伊、霍；

translations.literal: Moreover in the perilous autumn of Your Majesty's throne, you praised me as Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, or Huo Guang;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in the perilous autumn of Your Majesty's throne, you praised me as Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, or Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 既安之後，罵臣曰戎、羯、蕃、夷。

translations.literal: once secure you revile me as Rong, Jie, barbarian, or foreigner.
translations.idiomatic: Once secure you revile me as Rong, Jie, barbarian, or foreigner.

sentences.zh: 海內握兵立事如臣者眾矣，寧不懼陛下他時之罵哉？

translations.literal: Within the seas those who hold troops and stand on affairs like me are many—will they not fear Your Majesty's curses in future days?
translations.idiomatic: Within the seas those who hold troops and stand on affairs like me are many—will they not fear Your Majesty's curses in future days?

sentences.zh: 臣昨遇燕軍，以禮退舍。

translations.literal: Yesterday I met the Yan army and withdrew by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I met the Yan army and withdrew by ritual.

sentences.zh: 匡威淺昧，厚自矜誇，乃言臣中矢石，覆士卒。

translations.literal: Kuangwei was shallow and ignorant and greatly boasted himself, saying I was struck by arrow and stone and my soldiers were overrun.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei was shallow and ignorant and greatly boasted himself, saying I was struck by arrow and stone and my soldiers were overrun.

sentences.zh: 致內外吠聲一發，短謀競陳，誤陛下君臣之分。

translations.literal: Thus inside and outside barking arose at once, short plots competed in presentation, and the distinction between ruler and minister was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Thus inside and outside barking arose at once, short plots competed in presentation, and the distinction between ruler and minister was mistaken.

sentences.zh: 況命官選將，自有典刑，不必幸臣之弱而後取之。

translations.literal: Moreover appointing officials and selecting generals have their own canonical punishments—there is no need to take advantage of my weakness before seizing me.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover appointing officials and selecting generals have their own canonical punishments—there is no need to take advantage of my weakness before seizing me.

sentences.zh: 倘臣延期挺命，尚固一方，彼實何顏以見陛下。

translations.literal: If I should delay and defy orders, still holding one region firm—what face would they have to see Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: If I should delay and defy orders, still holding one region firm—what face would they have to see Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 此則姦邪朋黨，輕弄邦典，陛下凝旒端扆，何由知之？

translations.literal: This is wicked factions toying with state law—how would Your Majesty know, seated upright with curtain raised?
translations.idiomatic: This is wicked factions toying with state law—how would Your Majesty know, seated upright with curtain raised?

sentences.zh: 今張濬既以出軍，微臣固難束手。

translations.literal: Now that Zhang Jun has marched out, I truly cannot fold my hands.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Zhang Jun has marched out, I truly cannot fold my hands.

sentences.zh: 臣便欲叫閽，輕騎面叩玉階，訴邪佞於陛下之彤墀，納詔命於先皇之宗廟，然後束身司敗，甘處憲章。

translations.literal: I wish to cry at the gate, ride lightly to kneel on the jade steps, appeal against the wicked on Your Majesty's red court, and receive the edict at the former emperor's ancestral temple—then bind myself to the law and gladly accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to cry at the gate, ride lightly to kneel on the jade steps, appeal against the wicked on Your Majesty's red court, and receive the edict at the former emperor's ancestral temple—then bind myself to the law and gladly accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 時克用令所擒中使奉表，表至而濬敗，朝廷聳震，制曰：

translations.literal: At that time Keyong ordered the captured inner envoy to present the memorial; when the memorial arrived Jun was defeated, and the court was shaken. An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Keyong ordered the captured inner envoy to present the memorial. When the memorial arrived Jun was defeated, and the court was shaken. An edict said:

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫、門下侍郎、兼戸部尚書、同中書門下平章事、上柱國、清河郡開國伯、食邑一千二百戸、充河東行營諸道兵馬招討制置等使張濬，早以盛名，稱爲奇士，由是再加徵用，委以鈞衡，謂其必致小康，克勝大任。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Revenue, co-chancellor, pillar of state, Baron of Qinghe with a fief of twelve hundred households, overall commander of Hedong campaign armies—early famed as a remarkable man, and therefore repeatedly summoned and entrusted with the balance—yet he did not think to keep the Way but only sought merit, using unorthodox counsel to raise a nameless war.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Revenue, co-chancellor, pillar of state, Baron of Qinghe with a fief of twelve hundred households, overall commander of Hedong campaign armies—early famed as a remarkable man, and therefore repeatedly summoned and entrusted with the balance—yet he did not think to keep the Way but only sought merit, using unorthodox counsel to raise a nameless war.

sentences.zh: 而乃罔思守道，但欲邀功，用不詭之詢謀，起無名之兵革。

translations.literal: From the cloud a single stroke was to take only ten days; he firmly argued and momentum could not be turned.
translations.idiomatic: From the cloud a single stroke was to take only ten days; he firmly argued and momentum could not be turned.

sentences.zh: 自雲一舉，止在旬時，堅請抗論，勢莫能奪。

translations.literal: He slighted Zhuge Liang's campaign at Weibin and made small of Pei Du's march to Huaiyou.
translations.idiomatic: He slighted Zhuge Liang's campaign at Weibin and made small of Pei Du's march to Huaiyou.

sentences.zh: 輕葛亮渭濱之役，小裴度淮右之行。

translations.literal: Through cold and heat in the campaign, a million was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Through cold and heat in the campaign, a million was spent.

sentences.zh: 經功寒暄，耗費百萬。

translations.literal: Falsehood was manifest at court and in the wilds; deceit spread among Chinese and foreigners; no word of victory was heard while the prairie fire grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Falsehood was manifest at court and in the wilds. Deceit spread among Chinese and foreigners. No word of victory was heard while the prairie fire grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 虛誕彰於朝野，詐詭布於華夷，橫草蔑聞，燎原愈急。

translations.literal: Falsehood was manifest at court and in the wilds; deceit spread among Chinese and foreigners; no word of victory was heard while the prairie fire grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Falsehood was manifest at court and in the wilds. Deceit spread among Chinese and foreigners. No word of victory was heard while the prairie fire grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 俾擁旄乘驛之使，囚在虜庭；

translations.literal: He caused commissioners bearing banners to be imprisoned in the enemy court;
translations.idiomatic: He caused commissioners bearing banners to be imprisoned in the enemy court.

sentences.zh: 勤王奉國之軍，懷歸本土。

translations.literal: armies that aided the throne and served the state longed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Armies that aided the throne and served the state longed to return home.

sentences.zh: 忘廊廟之威重，結籓屏之仇讎。

translations.literal: He forgot the court's majesty and bound regional screens into enmity.
translations.idiomatic: He forgot the court's majesty and bound regional screens into enmity.

sentences.zh: 欲使海內生靈，竭其貢賦；

translations.literal: He wished to make the living within the seas exhaust their tribute;
translations.idiomatic: He wished to make the living within the seas exhaust their tribute.

sentences.zh: 不獨河中郡邑，蕩爲丘墟。

translations.literal: not only Hezhong's counties and towns were swept into ruins.
translations.idiomatic: not only Hezhong's counties and towns were swept into ruins.

sentences.zh: 潛生厲階，欲誰歸咎？

translations.literal: Secretly he bred the steps of disaster—upon whom shall blame be laid?
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he bred the steps of disaster—upon whom shall blame be laid?

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 征晁錯之故事，思王恢之舊章，國有明文，爾當何逭？

translations.literal: Invoking the precedent of Chao Cuo, reflecting on Wang Hui's old statutes—national law is clear; how can you escape?
translations.idiomatic: Invoking the precedent of Chao Cuo, reflecting on Wang Hui's old statutes—national law is clear. How can you escape?

sentences.zh: 尚以愛人以禮，理體宜然。

translations.literal: Still, in loving others by ritual, principle should be so.
translations.idiomatic: Still, in loving others by ritual, principle should be so.

sentences.zh: 廉鎮劇權，武昌善地，宜罷樞軸之務，仍停支度之司。

translations.literal: A taxing command is a good place at Wuchang; he should cease pivot affairs and also stop the treasury office.
translations.idiomatic: A taxing command is a good place at Wuchang. He should cease pivot affairs and also stop the treasury office.

sentences.zh: 勉自思惟，以逃後命。

translations.literal: Reflect earnestly to escape later judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Reflect earnestly to escape later judgment.

sentences.zh: 可檢校戸部尚書、鄂州刺史、武昌軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: He may be made acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of E Prefecture, and military governor and observer of the Wuchang army.
translations.idiomatic: He may be made acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of E Prefecture, and military governor and observer of the Wuchang army.

sentences.zh: 尋貶連州刺史，馳驛發遣。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted to Prefect of Lian Prefecture and sent by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to Prefect of Lian Prefecture and sent by express relay.

sentences.zh: 行至藍田關不行，留華州依韓建。

translations.literal: Reaching Lantian Pass he would not go on and stayed in Hua Prefecture relying on Han Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Lantian Pass he would not go on and stayed in Hua Prefecture relying on Han Jian.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷微弱，竟不能詰。

translations.literal: The court was then weak and ultimately could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then weak and ultimately could not investigate.

sentences.zh: 永寧縣吏葉彥者，張氏待之素厚。

translations.literal: Yongning County clerk Ye Yan had long been treated well by the Zhang family.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning County clerk Ye Yan had long been treated well by the Zhang family.

sentences.zh: 楊麟之來，彥知之，告濬第二子格曰：「相公之禍不可免，郎君宜自爲謀。」

translations.literal: When Yang Linzhi came, Yan knew it and told Jun's second son Ge: 'The chancellor's calamity cannot be avoided. Young master, you should plan for yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Linzhi came, Yan knew it and told Jun's second son Ge, "The chancellor's calamity cannot be avoided. Young master, you should plan for yourself."

sentences.zh: 格、濬父子號咷而已。

translations.literal: Ge and Jun father and son only wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Ge and Jun father and son only wailed.

sentences.zh: 濬謂格曰：「留則並命，去或可免。

translations.literal: Jun said to Ge: 'To stay is to die together; to go perhaps you may escape.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said to Ge, "To stay is to die together; to go perhaps you may escape.

sentences.zh: 汝自圖之，勿以吾爲累，冀存後祀也。」

translations.literal: Plan for yourself; do not take me as a burden, in hope of preserving later descendants.'
translations.idiomatic: Plan for yourself. Do not take me as a burden, in hope of preserving later descendants."

sentences.zh: 格拜辭而去。

translations.literal: Ge bowed in farewell and left.
translations.idiomatic: Ge bowed in farewell and left.

sentences.zh: 葉彥率義士三十人，送渡漢江而旋。

translations.literal: Ye Yan led thirty righteous men, escorted them across the Han River and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yan led thirty righteous men, escorted them across the Han River and returned.

sentences.zh: 格由荊江上峽入蜀。

translations.literal: Ge went up the gorges from the Jing River into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Ge went up the gorges from the Jing River into Shu.

sentences.zh: 王建僭號，用爲宰相。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian usurped title, he used Ge as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian usurped title, he used Ge as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 中興平蜀，任圜攜格而還。

translations.literal: When restoration pacified Shu, Ren Yuan brought Ge back.
translations.idiomatic: When restoration pacified Shu, Ren Yuan brought Ge back.

sentences.zh: 格感葉彥之惠，訪之，身已歿，而厚報其家。

translations.literal: Ge, grateful for Ye Yan's kindness, sought him out; Yan had already died, yet he richly rewarded the family.
translations.idiomatic: Ge, grateful for Ye Yan's kindness, sought him out. Yan had already died, yet he richly rewarded the family.

sentences.zh: 濬第三子竄於楊行密。

translations.literal: Jun's third son fled to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's third son fled to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 自乾寧之後，賊臣內侮，王室浸微。

translations.literal: After the Qianning reign, treacherous ministers insulted within and the royal house gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianning reign, treacherous ministers insulted within and the royal house gradually weakened.

sentences.zh: 昭宗不堪淩弱，欲簡拔奇材以爲相。

translations.literal: Zhaozong could not bear being bullied and wished to select extraordinary talent as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong could not bear being bullied and wished to select extraordinary talent as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 然采於群小之論，未嘗獲一名人。

translations.literal: Yet taking from the talk of petty men, he never obtained a famous person.
translations.idiomatic: Yet taking from the talk of petty men, he never obtained a famous person.

sentences.zh: 登用之徒，無不爲時嗤誚。

translations.literal: Those elevated and used were all mocked by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Those elevated and used were all mocked by the age.

sentences.zh: 朱朴者，乾寧中爲國子博士。

translations.literal: Zhu Pu, in the Qianning reign was Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Pu, in the Qianning reign was Doctor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 腐儒木強，無他才伎。

translations.literal: A pedantic scholar, wooden and obstinate, without other talent.
translations.idiomatic: A pedantic scholar, wooden and obstinate, without other talent.

sentences.zh: 道士許巖士出入禁中，嘗依朴爲姦利，從容上前薦僕有經濟才。

translations.literal: Daoist priest Xu Yanshi entered the forbidden precincts, often relying on Pu for illicit profit, and casually before the throne recommended the servant's economic talent.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priest Xu Yanshi entered the forbidden precincts, often relying on Pu for illicit profit, and casually before the throne recommended the servant's economic talent.

sentences.zh: 昭宗召見，對以經義，甚悅，即日拜諫議大夫、平章事。

translations.literal: Zhaozong summoned and questioned him on classical meaning and was greatly pleased; the same day he was made Remonstrating Official and co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong summoned and questioned him on classical meaning and was greatly pleased. The same day he was made Remonstrating Official and co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 在中書與名公齒，筆劄議論，動爲笑端。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat he ranked with famous grandees; letters and discussion were constantly laughed at.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat he ranked with famous grandees. Letters and discussion were constantly laughed at.

sentences.zh: 數月，巖士事敗，俱爲韓建所殺。

translations.literal: Within months Yanshi's affair failed and both were killed by Han Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Yanshi's affair failed and both were killed by Han Jian.

sentences.zh: 鄭綮者，以進士登第，歷監察、殿中，倉、戸二員外，金、刑、右司三郎中。

translations.literal: Zheng Qi passed the jinshi examination and successively served as investigating censor, palace censor, vice directors of the granary and revenue bureaus, and directors of the gold, punishment, and right bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qi passed the jinshi examination and successively served as investigating censor, palace censor, vice directors of the granary and revenue bureaus, and directors of the gold, punishment, and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 家貧求郡，出爲廬州刺史。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he sought a prefecture; he went out as Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and he sought a prefecture. He went out as Prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 黃巢自嶺表還，經淮南剽掠。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao returned from south of the ranges he plundered through Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao returned from south of the ranges he plundered through Huainan.

sentences.zh: 綮移黃巢文牒，請不犯郡界。

translations.literal: Qi forwarded Huang Chao's document asking that the prefectural border not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Qi forwarded Huang Chao's document asking that the prefectural border not be violated.

sentences.zh: 巢笑而從之，一郡獨不被寇。

translations.literal: Chao laughed and complied; that prefecture alone was not raided.
translations.idiomatic: Chao laughed and complied. That prefecture alone was not raided.

sentences.zh: 天子嘉之，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven praised this and gave crimson fish bags.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this and gave crimson fish bags.

sentences.zh: 罷郡，有錢千緡，寄州帑。

translations.literal: When he left the prefecture he had a thousand strings of cash deposited in the prefectural treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the prefecture he had a thousand strings of cash deposited in the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 後郡數陷，盜不犯鄭使君寄庫錢。

translations.literal: Later the prefecture fell several times, yet thieves did not touch Commissioner Zheng's deposited money.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prefecture fell several times, yet thieves did not touch Commissioner Zheng's deposited money.

sentences.zh: 至楊行密爲刺史，送所寄於京師還綮。

translations.literal: When Yang Xingmi became prefect he sent what was deposited to the capital and returned it to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmi became prefect he sent what was deposited to the capital and returned it to Qi.

sentences.zh: 綮善爲詩，多侮劇刺時，故落格調，時號鄭五歇後體。

translations.literal: Qi was good at poetry and often mocked and satirized the times; therefore he fell from standard tone, and the age called him Zheng the Fifth's postscript style.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was good at poetry and often mocked and satirized the times. Therefore he fell from standard tone, and the age called him Zheng the Fifth's postscript style.

sentences.zh: 初去廬江，與郡人別云：「唯有兩行公廨淚，一時灑向渡頭風。」

translations.literal: When he first left Lujiang he parted from the prefectural people saying: 'Only two lines of official tears, at once scattered to the ferry wind.'
translations.idiomatic: When he first left Lujiang he parted from the prefectural people saying, "Only two lines of official tears, at once scattered to the ferry wind."

sentences.zh: 滑稽皆此類也。

translations.literal: His humor was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His humor was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 王徽爲御史大夫，奏綮爲兵部郎中、知臺雜，遷給事中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Wang Hui as Censor-in-Chief memorialized Qi as Director of the Bureau of War and handler of censorial miscellaneous affairs; he was promoted to Attendant and given gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui as Censor-in-Chief memorialized Qi as Director of the Bureau of War and handler of censorial miscellaneous affairs. He was promoted to Attendant and given gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自山南還，以宰相杜讓能弟弘徽爲中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shannan, Chancellor Du Rangneng's younger brother Honghui was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shannan, Chancellor Du Rangneng's younger brother Honghui was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 綮以弘徽兄在中書，弟不宜同居禁近，封還制書。

translations.literal: Qi, because Honghui's elder brother was in the Secretariat and the younger should not dwell together in the forbidden proximity, returned the edict sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, because Honghui's elder brother was in the Secretariat and the younger should not dwell together in the forbidden proximity, returned the edict sealed.

sentences.zh: 天子不報，綮即移病休官。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven did not reply; Qi immediately pleaded illness and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply. Qi immediately pleaded illness and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 無幾，以左散騎常侍征還。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back as Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned back as Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 朝政有闕，無不上章論列。

translations.literal: Whenever court affairs had faults he memorialized without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever court affairs had faults he memorialized without fail.

sentences.zh: 事雖不行，喧傳都下，執政惡之，改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Though affairs did not proceed, they were loudly spread in the capital; the chief ministers hated this and changed him to Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Though affairs did not proceed, they were loudly spread in the capital. The chief ministers hated this and changed him to Chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 物議以綮匡諫而置之散地，不可，執政懼，復用爲常侍。

translations.literal: Public opinion held that Qi was remonstrating yet placed in an idle post—this would not do; the chief ministers feared this and again used him as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Qi was remonstrating yet placed in an idle post—this would not do. The chief ministers feared this and again used him as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 光化初，昭宗還宮，庶政未愜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guanghua, Zhaozong returned to the palace; many affairs were not yet satisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guanghua, Zhaozong returned to the palace. Many affairs were not yet satisfactory.

sentences.zh: 綮每形於詩什而嘲之，中人或誦其語於上前。

translations.literal: Qi often showed it in poems mocking them; inner attendants sometimes recited his words before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Qi often showed it in poems mocking them. Inner attendants sometimes recited his words before the throne.

sentences.zh: 昭宗見其激訐，謂有蘊蓄，就常奏班簿側註云：「鄭綮可禮部侍郎、平章事。」

translations.literal: Zhaozong saw his sharp criticism and thought he had stored capacity; beside the regular attendance roster he annotated: 'Zheng Qi may be Vice Minister of Rites and co-chancellor.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong saw his sharp criticism and thought he had stored capacity. Beside the regular attendance roster he annotated, "Zheng Qi may be Vice Minister of Rites and co-chancellor."

sentences.zh: 中書胥吏詣其家參謁，綮笑而問之曰：「諸君大誤，俾天下人並不識字，宰相不及鄭五也。」

translations.literal: Secretariat clerks came to his house to pay respects; Qi laughed and asked them: 'You gentlemen are greatly mistaken, making the people of the realm all illiterate—even the chancellor cannot match Zheng the Fifth.'
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat clerks came to his house to pay respects. Qi laughed and asked them, "You gentlemen are greatly mistaken, making the people of the realm all illiterate—even the chancellor cannot match Zheng the Fifth."

sentences.zh: 胥吏曰：「出自聖旨特恩，來日制下。」

translations.literal: The clerks said: 'It comes from special grace in the imperial edict; tomorrow the decree will issue.'
translations.idiomatic: The clerks said, "It comes from special grace in the imperial edict. Tomorrow the decree will issue."

sentences.zh: 抗其手曰：「萬一如此，笑殺他人。」

translations.literal: He resisted their hands: 'If by any chance it is so, it will kill others with laughter.'
translations.idiomatic: He resisted their hands. "If by any chance it is so, it will kill others with laughter."

sentences.zh: 明日果制下，親賓來賀，搔首言曰：「歇後鄭五作宰相，時事可知矣。」

translations.literal: The next day the decree indeed issued; relatives and guests came to congratulate. He scratched his head and said: 'Postscript Zheng the Fifth as chancellor—the affairs of the age can be known.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day the decree indeed issued. Relatives and guests came to congratulate. He scratched his head and said, "Postscript Zheng the Fifth as chancellor—the affairs of the age can be known."

sentences.zh: 累表遜讓，不獲。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to decline and could not obtain permission.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized to decline and could not obtain permission.

sentences.zh: 既入視事，侃然守道，無復詼諧。

translations.literal: Once he entered to handle affairs he stood upright and kept the Way, with no more jest.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered to handle affairs he stood upright and kept the Way, with no more jest.

sentences.zh: 終以物望非宜，自求引退。

translations.literal: Ultimately because public expectation was not fitting he asked to withdraw of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ultimately because public expectation was not fitting he asked to withdraw of himself.

sentences.zh: 三月餘，移疾乞骸，以太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: After more than three months he pleaded illness and asked to retire, retiring as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After more than three months he pleaded illness and asked to retire, retiring as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 時議以昭宗命臺臣濬、朴、綮三人尤謬，季末之妖也。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time held that Zhaozong's appointment of the censorial ministers Jun, Pu, and Qi was especially absurd—a portent of the dynasty's end.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion of the time held that Zhaozong's appointment of the censorial ministers Jun, Pu, and Qi was especially absurd—a portent of the dynasty's end.

sentences.zh: 劉崇望，字希徒。

translations.literal: Liu Chongwang, style name Xitu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chongwang, whose courtesy name was Xitu.

sentences.zh: 其先代郡人，隨元魏孝文帝徙洛陽，遂爲河南人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were natives of Dai Prefecture; with Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei they moved to Luoyang and thus became Henan people.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were natives of Dai Prefecture. With Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei they moved to Luoyang and thus became Henan people.

sentences.zh: 八代祖隋大理卿坦，生政會，輔太宗起義晉陽，官至戸部尚書，封渝國公，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Tan of Sui served as Director of the Court of Judicial Review; he begot Zhenghui, who aided Emperor Taizong in raising righteousness at Jinyang, served to Minister of Revenue, was enfeoffed as Duke of Yu, and had his image in Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Tan of Sui served as Director of the Court of Judicial Review. Tan begot Zhenghui, who aided Emperor Taizong in raising righteousness at Jinyang, served to Minister of Revenue, was enfeoffed as Duke of Yu, and had his image in Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 政會生玄意，尚太宗女南平公主，歷洪、饒八州采訪使。

translations.literal: Zhenghui begot Xuanyi, who married Emperor Taizong's daughter the Princess of Nanping and served as investigating commissioner of eight prefectures including Hong and Rao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghui begot Xuanyi, who married Emperor Taizong's daughter the Princess of Nanping and served as investigating commissioner of eight prefectures including Hong and Rao.

sentences.zh: 玄意生奇，位至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xuanyi begot Qi, who served to vice minister of civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyi begot Qi, who served to vice minister of civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 奇生慎知，仕至獲嘉令。

translations.literal: Qi begot Shenzhi, who served to magistrate of Huojia.
translations.idiomatic: Qi begot Shenzhi, who served to magistrate of Huojia.

sentences.zh: 慎知生褧，仕至東阿令。

translations.literal: Shenzhi begot Ying, who served to magistrate of Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi begot Ying, who served to magistrate of Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 褧生藻，位終秘書郎。

translations.literal: Ying begot Zao, who served to Secretariat Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Ying begot Zao, who served to Secretariat Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 藻生符，進士登第，咸通中位終蔡州刺史，生八子：崇龜、崇望、崇魯、崇謨最知名。

translations.literal: Zao begot Fu, who passed the jinshi and in the Xiantong reign served to Prefect of Cai; he had eight sons—Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo were most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zao begot Fu, who passed the jinshi and in the Xiantong reign served to Prefect of Cai. He had eight sons—Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo were most renowned.

sentences.zh: 崇龜，進士擢第，累遷起居舍人，禮部、兵部二員外。

translations.literal: Chonggui passed the jinshi, was repeatedly promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions and vice minister of rites and war.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui passed the jinshi, was repeatedly promoted to Recorder of the Emperor's Actions and vice minister of rites and war.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed on mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 春，鄭從讜罷相，鎮太原，奏崇龜爲度支判官、檢校吏部郎中、御史中丞，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In spring, when Zheng Congdang was removed as chancellor and governed Taiyuan, he memorialized Chonggui as treasury adjutant, acting director of the Bureau of Civil Affairs, and vice censor, and gave gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, when Zheng Congdang was removed as chancellor and governed Taiyuan, he memorialized Chonggui as treasury adjutant, acting director of the Bureau of Civil Affairs, and vice censor, and gave gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 入朝，爲兵部郎中，拜給事中。

translations.literal: Entering court he was Director of the Bureau of War and made Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Entering court he was Director of the Bureau of War and made Attendant.

sentences.zh: 大順中，遷左散騎常侍、集賢殿學士、判院事，改戸部侍郎，檢校戸部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Datong reign he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant, academician of the Jixian Hall, and director of the institute; changed to vice minister of revenue and acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong reign he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant, academician of the Jixian Hall, and director of the institute. He was changed to vice minister of revenue and acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出爲廣州刺史、清海軍節度、嶺南東道觀察處置等使，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Guang Prefecture, military governor of the Qinghai army, and governor-general of Lingnan East Circuit; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Prefect of Guang Prefecture, military governor of the Qinghai army, and governor-general of Lingnan East Circuit. He died.

sentences.zh: 崇望，登進士科。

translations.literal: Chongwang passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwang passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 王凝廉問宣歙，辟爲轉運巡官。

translations.literal: Wang Ning investigated Xu and She and recruited him as transport patrol officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ning investigated Xu and She and recruited him as transport patrol officer.

sentences.zh: 戸部侍郎裴坦領鹽鐵，辟爲參佐。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Tan oversaw salt and iron and recruited him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Tan oversaw salt and iron and recruited him as aide.

sentences.zh: 崔安潛鎮許昌、成都，崇望昆仲四人，皆在安潛幕下。

translations.literal: When Cui Anqian governed Xuchang and Chengdu, four Chong brothers were all in Anqian's staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Anqian governed Xuchang and Chengdu, four Chong brothers were all in Anqian's staff.

sentences.zh: 入爲長安尉，直弘文館，遷監察御史、右補闕、起居郎、弘文館學士，轉司勛、吏部二員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered as magistrate of Chang'an, direct scholar of the Hongwen Hall, and was promoted to investigating censor, Right Supplicator, Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, and academician of the Hongwen Hall; transferred to vice directors of the Bureau of Merit and the Bureau of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as magistrate of Chang'an, direct scholar of the Hongwen Hall, and was promoted to investigating censor, Right Supplicator, Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, and academician of the Hongwen Hall. He was transferred to vice directors of the Bureau of Merit and the Bureau of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 崔安潛爲吏部尚書，崇望判南曹，滌除宿弊，復清選部。

translations.literal: When Cui Anqian was Minister of Civil Affairs, Chongwang judged the Southern Bureau, cleansing long-standing abuses and restoring the pure selection department.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Anqian was Minister of Civil Affairs, Chongwang judged the Southern Bureau, cleansing long-standing abuses and restoring the pure selection department.

sentences.zh: 田令孜幹政，籓鎮怨望，河中尤甚，不修職貢。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi interfered in government; regional commands resented it—Hezhong especially did not repair tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi interfered in government. Regional commands resented it—Hezhong especially did not repair tribute duties.

sentences.zh: 僖宗在山南，以蒲阪近關，欲其效用，選使諭旨，以崇望爲諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong was in Shannan; because Puzhou was near the pass he wished it effective and selected an envoy to explain the intent, making Chongwang Remonstrating Official.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong was in Shannan. Because Puzhou was near the pass he wished it effective and selected an envoy to explain the intent, making Chongwang Remonstrating Official.

sentences.zh: 既至，諭以大義，重榮奉詔恭順，誓心匡復，請殺朱玫自贖。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he explained the great principle; Chongrong respectfully obeyed the edict, vowed to restore the realm, and asked to kill Zhu Mei to atone.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he explained the great principle. Chongrong respectfully obeyed the edict, vowed to restore the realm, and asked to kill Zhu Mei to atone.

sentences.zh: 使還，上悅，召入翰林充學士，累遷戸部侍郎、承旨，轉兵部，在禁署四年。

translations.literal: Returning from the mission the emperor was pleased and summoned him to the Hanlin, repeatedly promoting him to vice minister of revenue and chief academician, then to war; he was in the forbidden secretariat four years.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the mission the emperor was pleased and summoned him to the Hanlin, repeatedly promoting him to vice minister of revenue and chief academician, then to war. He was in the forbidden secretariat four years.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，拜中書侍郎、同平章事，累兼兵部、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong took the throne he was made vice director of the Secretariat and co-chancellor, cumulatively holding the ministries of war and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong took the throne he was made vice director of the Secretariat and co-chancellor, cumulatively holding the ministries of war and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 大順初，同列張濬畫策討太原，崇望以爲不可，濬果敗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, fellow minister Zhang Jun plotted to attack Taiyuan; Chongwang thought it could not be done and Jun indeed failed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong, fellow minister Zhang Jun plotted to attack Taiyuan. Chongwang thought it could not be done and Jun indeed failed.

sentences.zh: 濬黜，崇望代爲門下侍郎、監修國史、判度支。

translations.literal: When Jun was removed, Chongwang replaced him as vice director of the Secretariat, supervisor of the national history, and in charge of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was removed, Chongwang replaced him as vice director of the Secretariat, supervisor of the national history, and in charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 明年，玉山都頭楊守信協楊復恭稱兵闕下，陣於通化門。

translations.literal: The next year Yushan command head Yang Shouxin joined Yang Fugong in raising troops below the palace and arrayed at Tonghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yushan command head Yang Shouxin joined Yang Fugong in raising troops below the palace and arrayed at Tonghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 上陳兵於延嘉門。

translations.literal: The emperor arrayed troops at Yanjia Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor arrayed troops at Yanjia Gate.

sentences.zh: 是夜，命崇望守度支庫。

translations.literal: That night he ordered Chongwang to guard the treasury storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: That night he ordered Chongwang to guard the treasury storehouse.

sentences.zh: 明日曉，入含光門。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he entered Hanguang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day he entered Hanguang Gate.

sentences.zh: 未開，門內禁軍列於左右，俟門開即劫掠兩市。

translations.literal: Before it opened, forbidden troops within lined left and right, waiting for the gate to open to plunder both markets.
translations.idiomatic: Before it opened, forbidden troops within lined left and right, waiting for the gate to open to plunder both markets.

sentences.zh: 及聞傳呼宰相來，門方啟，崇望駐馬慰諭之曰：「聖上在街東親總戎事。

translations.literal: When they heard the call that the chancellor was coming, the gate just opened; Chongwang halted his horse and comforted them: 'The sage is east of the street personally directing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard the call that the chancellor was coming, the gate just opened. Chongwang halted his horse and comforted them, "The sage is east of the street personally directing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 公等禁軍，何不樓前殺賊，立取功名。

translations.literal: You forbidden troops—why not kill the bandits before the tower and win merit at once?
translations.idiomatic: You forbidden troops—why not kill the bandits before the tower and win merit at once?

sentences.zh: 切不可剽掠街市，圖小利以成惡名也。」

translations.literal: You must not plunder the markets for small gain and make a bad name.'
translations.idiomatic: You must not plunder the markets for small gain and make a bad name."

sentences.zh: 將士唯唯，從崇望至長樂門。

translations.literal: The soldiers assented and followed Chongwang to Changle Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers assented and followed Chongwang to Changle Gate.

sentences.zh: 守信見兵來，即遁去，軍士呼萬歲。

translations.literal: When Shouxin saw troops coming he fled at once; the soldiers shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouxin saw troops coming he fled at once. The soldiers shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 是日庫市獲全，軍人不亂，繄崇望之方略也。

translations.literal: That day the treasury and markets were preserved and the soldiers did not riot—it was Chongwang's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: That day the treasury and markets were preserved and the soldiers did not riot—it was Chongwang's strategy.

sentences.zh: 尋加左僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 時溥與朱全忠爭衡，全忠謀兼徐、泗，上表請以重臣鎮徐，乃以崇望守本官，充武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shi Pu and Zhu Quanzhong contended; Quanzhong plotted to annex Xu and Si and memorialized asking that a weighty minister govern Xu; Chongwang was ordered to keep his office and serve as military governor of the Wuning army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu and Zhu Quanzhong contended. Quanzhong plotted to annex Xu and Si and memorialized asking that a weighty minister govern Xu. Chongwang was ordered to keep his office and serve as military governor of the Wuning army.

sentences.zh: 溥不受代，行至華陰而還，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: Pu would not accept replacement; reaching Hua Pass he returned and was made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Pu would not accept replacement. Reaching Hua Pass he returned and was made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 王重盈死，王珂、王珙爭河中節鉞，朝廷以宰相崔胤爲河中節度使。

translations.literal: When Wang Chongying died, Wang Ke and Wang Gong contended for the Hezhong command; the court made Chancellor Cui Yin military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chongying died, Wang Ke and Wang Gong contended for the Hezhong command. The court made Chancellor Cui Yin military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 珂，李克用之子婿也。

translations.literal: Ke was Li Keyong's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was Li Keyong's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 河東進奏官薛志勤揚言曰：「崔相雖重德，如作鎮河中代王珂，不如光德劉公，於我公事素也。」

translations.literal: Hedong memorial-presenting official Xue Zhiqin proclaimed: "Though Chancellor Cui is weighty in virtue, if he garrisons Hezhong in Wang Ke's place, he is not as good as Lord Liu of Guangde, who has long handled our official affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Hedong memorial-presenting official Xue Zhiqin proclaimed, "Though Chancellor Cui is weighty in virtue, if he garrisons Hezhong in Wang Ke's place, he is not as good as Lord Liu of Guangde, who has long handled our official affairs."

sentences.zh: 及三鎮以兵入朝，殺害大臣，以志勤之言，責授崇望昭州司馬。

translations.literal: When Wang Xingyu was executed Taiyuan memorialized that Chongwang was innocently exiled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xingyu was executed Taiyuan memorialized that Chongwang was innocently exiled.

sentences.zh: 及王行瑜誅，太原上表言崇望無辜放逐。

translations.literal: He had already reached Jingnan when an edict recalled him and made him Minister of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had already reached Jingnan when an edict recalled him and made him Minister of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時已至荊南，有詔召還，拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Before he arrived Wang Pu again handled state affairs and concurrently was Minister of Civil Affairs; Chongwang was changed to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived Wang Pu again handled state affairs and concurrently was Minister of Civil Affairs. Chongwang was changed to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 未至，王溥再知政事，兼吏部尚書，乃改崇望兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At that time Xichuan invaded Gu Yanhui, wishing to annex Dongchuan; Chongwang was made acting Right Vice Director, co-chancellor, Prefect of Zi, and military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xichuan invaded Gu Yanhui, wishing to annex Dongchuan. Chongwang was made acting Right Vice Director, co-chancellor, Prefect of Zi, and military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時西川侵寇顧彥暉，欲並東川，以崇望檢校右僕射、平章事、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: Before reaching his command he was recalled and again made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching his command he was recalled and again made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 未至鎮，召還，復爲兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age sixty-two and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年六十二，冊贈司空。

translations.literal: Chonglu passed the jinshi; Zheng Congdang memorialized him as Taiyuan investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglu passed the jinshi. Zheng Congdang memorialized him as Taiyuan investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 崇魯，登進士第，鄭從讜奏充太原推官。

translations.literal: At that time his elder brother Chonggui was circuit adjutant; the brothers dwelt together in the staff office and soon he was transferred to chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his elder brother Chonggui was circuit adjutant. The brothers dwelt together in the staff office and soon he was transferred to chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 時兄崇龜爲節度判官，昆仲同居幕府，尋轉掌書記。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe he entered court as Right Reminder and Left Supplicator.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhonghe he entered court as Right Reminder and Left Supplicator.

sentences.zh: 中和二年入朝，拜右拾遺、左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingfu he was vice director of the Bureau of Works and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingfu he was vice director of the Bureau of Works and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 景福初，以水部員外郎知制誥。

translations.literal: In the second year, when Du Rangneng was guilty, Zhaozong again appointed Wei Zhaodu chancellor and Hanlin academician Li Xi co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Du Rangneng was guilty, Zhaozong again appointed Wei Zhaodu chancellor and Hanlin academician Li Xi co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 二年，杜讓能得罪，昭宗復命韋昭度爲相，翰林學士李谿同平章事。

translations.literal: Chonglu was friendly with Cui Zhaowei.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglu was friendly with Cui Zhaowei.

sentences.zh: 崇魯與崔昭緯相善。

translations.literal: Zhaowei relied on Bin and Qi's support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowei relied on Bin and Qi's support.

sentences.zh: 昭緯恃邠、岐之援。

translations.literal: After Rangneng was executed power returned to himself; Zhaozong favored Li Xi for literature and feared that if Xi held office and won favor imperial regard would gradually fade; he therefore privately plotted with Chonglu to obstruct it.
translations.idiomatic: After Rangneng was executed power returned to himself. Zhaozong favored Li Xi for literature and feared that if Xi held office and won favor imperial regard would gradually fade. He therefore privately plotted with Chonglu to obstruct it.

sentences.zh: 讓能既誅之後，權歸於己，昭宗師李谿爲文，懼居位得寵則恩顧漸衰，乃私與崇魯謀沮之。

translations.literal: After Rangneng was executed, power fell to him. Zhaozong took Li Xi as his literary tutor; fearing that once Xi held office and favor, grace toward him would gradually fade, he privately plotted with Chonglu to obstruct it.
translations.idiomatic: After Rangneng was executed, power fell to him. Zhaozong took Li Xi as his literary tutor; fearing that once Xi held office and favor, grace toward him would gradually fade, he privately plotted with Chonglu to obstruct it.

sentences.zh: 及谿宣制之日，出班而哭，謂昭緯曰：「朝廷雖乏賢，不可用纖人爲宰輔。

translations.literal: On the day Xi proclaimed the edict he left the ranks weeping and said to Zhaowei: "Though the court lacks talent, one cannot use a petty man as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xi proclaimed the edict he left the ranks weeping and said to Zhaowei, "Though the court lacks talent, one cannot use a petty man as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 谿比依復恭、重遂居內職。

translations.literal: The other day Grand Marshal Du was in disgrace—the court was deeply shamed.
translations.idiomatic: The other day Grand Marshal Du was in disgrace—the court was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 前日杜太尉狼籍，爲朝廷深恥。

translations.literal: Now weakened thus, how can we again follow an overturned cart track?
translations.idiomatic: Now weakened thus, how can we again follow an overturned cart track?

sentences.zh: 今則削弱如此，安可更遵覆轍乎？」

translations.literal: Now weakened thus, how can we again follow an overturned cart track?"
translations.idiomatic: Now weakened thus, how can we again follow an overturned cart track?"

sentences.zh: 由是谿命不行。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xi's appointment did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xi's appointment did not proceed.

sentences.zh: 谿自十一月初至歲暮，聯上十表訴冤，其詞詆毀，所不忍聞。

translations.literal: The next spring Xi was again appointed co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Xi was again appointed co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 明年春，復命谿爲平章事。

translations.literal: Zhaowei summoned Li Maozhen, Wang Xingyu, and Han Jian to raise troops and enter court, killing Zhaodu and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaowei summoned Li Maozhen, Wang Xingyu, and Han Jian to raise troops and enter court, killing Zhaodu and Xi.

sentences.zh: 昭緯召李茂貞、王行瑜、韓建稱兵入朝，殺昭度與谿。

translations.literal: That year Taiyuan executed Wang Xingyu; Zhaowei was demoted and Chonglu was implicated and demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taiyuan executed Wang Xingyu. Zhaowei was demoted and Chonglu was implicated and demoted to registrar of Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其年，太原誅王行瑜，昭緯貶官，崇魯坐貶崖州司戸。

translations.literal: That year Taiyuan executed Wang Xingyu; Zhaowei was demoted, and Chonglu was implicated and demoted to clerk of Yaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taiyuan executed Wang Xingyu; Zhaowei was demoted, and Chonglu was implicated and demoted to clerk of Yaizhou.

sentences.zh: 初崇龜在外，聞崇魯哭麻，大恚，數日不食，謂所親曰：「吾家兄弟進身有素，未嘗以聲利敗名。

translations.literal: When Chonggui was abroad and heard Chonglu wept at the hemp edict, he was greatly angry, for several days ate nothing, and said to intimates: "Our family's brothers rose by standard paths and never ruined their names for sound and profit.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonggui was abroad and heard Chonglu wept at the hemp edict, he was greatly angry, for several days ate nothing, and said to intimates, "Our family's brothers rose by standard paths and never ruined their names for sound and profit.

sentences.zh: 吾門不幸，生此等兒。」

translations.literal: Our gate is unfortunate to bear such a son."
translations.idiomatic: Our gate is unfortunate to bear such a son."

sentences.zh: 崇謨，進士及第。

translations.literal: Chongmo passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Chongmo passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 乾寧末，爲太常少卿、弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: Xu Yanruo was a descendant of the Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yougong of Empress Wu's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanruo was a descendant of the Director of the Court of Judicial Review Yougong of Empress Wu's reign.

sentences.zh: 徐彥若，天后朝大理卿有功之裔。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Zai, grandfather Tao, father Shang—three generations in succession passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Zai, grandfather Tao, father Shang—three generations in succession passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖宰，祖陶，父商，三世繼登進士科。

translations.literal: Shang, style name Yisheng, passed the examination, took his first office as proofreader in the Secretariat.
