translations.idiomatic: Shang, whose courtesy name was Yisheng, passed the examination and took his first office as proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 商，字義聲，及第，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attending Censor and changed to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Attending Censor and changed to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍御史，改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was drafter of edicts, transferred to director, summoned as Hanlin academician, made Vice Director of the Secretariat and vice minister of revenue in charge of that ministry, acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of Xiang, and military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was drafter of edicts, transferred to director, summoned as Hanlin academician, made Vice Director of the Secretariat and vice minister of revenue in charge of that ministry, acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of Xiang, and military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋知制誥，轉郎中，召充翰林學士，拜中書舍人、戸部侍郎判本司事，檢校戸部尚書、襄州刺史、山南東道節度等使。

translations.literal: He entered as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 入爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was made Minister of Punishments and commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits; promoted to Minister of War, Viscount of Dongguan with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiantong he was made Minister of Punishments and commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits. He was promoted to Minister of War, Viscount of Dongguan with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，加刑部尚書，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使，遷兵部尚書、東莞子、食邑五百戸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, with his existing office he became co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, with his existing office he became co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 四年，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was removed as chancellor, made acting Right Vice Director, Governor of Jiangling, and military governor and observer of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was removed as chancellor, made acting Right Vice Director, Governor of Jiangling, and military governor and observer of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 六年罷相，檢校右僕射、江陵尹、荊南節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: He entered as Minister of Civil Affairs, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Minister of Civil Affairs, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and died.

sentences.zh: 入爲吏部尚書，累遷太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: Yanruo passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanruo passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 彥若，進士擢第。

translations.literal: Yanruo passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanruo passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，以尚書郎知制誥，正拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu he was Director of a Bureau and drafter of edicts, and formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qianfu he was Director of a Bureau and drafter of edicts, and formally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，遷御史中丞，轉吏部侍郎，檢校戸部尚書，代李茂貞爲鳳翔隴節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong took the throne he was promoted to vice censor, transferred to vice minister of civil affairs, acting Minister of Revenue, and replaced Li Maozhen as military governor of Fengxiang and Long.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong took the throne he was promoted to vice censor, transferred to vice minister of civil affairs, acting Minister of Revenue, and replaced Li Maozhen as military governor of Fengxiang and Long.

sentences.zh: 茂貞不受代，復拜中丞，改兵部侍郎、同平章事，進加中書侍郎，累兼左僕射、監修國史。

translations.literal: Maozhen would not accept replacement; Yanruo was again made vice censor, changed to vice minister of war and co-chancellor, promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, and cumulatively held Left Vice Director and supervisor of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen would not accept replacement. Yanruo was again made vice censor, changed to vice minister of war and co-chancellor, promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, and cumulatively held Left Vice Director and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 扈昭宗石門還宮，加開府儀同三司、守司空，進封齊國公，太清宮、修奉太廟等使，加弘文館大學士，賜「扶危匡國致理功臣」名。

translations.literal: Escorting Zhaozong from Shimen back to the palace he was made Grand General of the Palace Guard, acting Minister of Works, advanced to Duke of Qi, commissioner of the Grand Pure Temple and repair of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and given the title 'Meritorious Minister Who Supported Peril, Restored the State, and Brought Order.'
translations.idiomatic: Escorting Zhaozong from Shimen back to the palace he was made Grand General of the Palace Guard, acting Minister of Works, advanced to Duke of Qi, commissioner of the Grand Pure Temple and repair of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and given the title 'Meritorious Minister Who Supported Peril, Restored the State, and Brought Order.'

sentences.zh: 昭宗自華還宮，進位太保、門下侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong returned from Hua to the palace he was promoted to Grand Mentor and vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong returned from Hua to the palace he was promoted to Grand Mentor and vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤專權，以彥若在己上，欲事權萃於其門。

translations.literal: At that time Cui Yin monopolized power; because Yanruo was above him he wished to concentrate authority in his own faction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cui Yin monopolized power. Because Yanruo was above him he wished to concentrate authority in his own faction.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，以彥若檢校太尉、同平章事、廣州刺史、清海軍節度、嶺南東道節度等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year Yanruo was made acting Grand Marshal, co-chancellor, Prefect of Guang, military governor of the Qinghai army, and governor-general of Lingnan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year Yanruo was made acting Grand Marshal, co-chancellor, Prefect of Guang, military governor of the Qinghai army, and governor-general of Lingnan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮。

translations.literal: He died in his command.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his command.

sentences.zh: 弟彥樞，位至太常少卿。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yanshu served to Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yanshu served to Vice Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 子綰，天祐初歷司勛、兵部二員外，戸部、兵部二郎中。

translations.literal: His son Wan, in the early Tiansheng reign successively served as vice directors of the Bureau of Merit and Bureau of War and directors of the revenue and war bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan, in the early Tiansheng reign successively served as vice directors of the Bureau of Merit and Bureau of War and directors of the revenue and war bureaus.

sentences.zh: 陸扆，字祥文，本名允迪，吳郡人。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, style name Xiangwen, original name Yundi, was a native of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, whose courtesy name was Xiangwen and whose original name was Yundi, came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 徙家於陜，今爲陜州人。

translations.literal: The family moved to Shan and is now Shan Prefecture people.
translations.idiomatic: The family moved to Shan and is now Shan Prefecture people.

sentences.zh: 曾祖澧，位終殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Li served to Attending Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Li served to Attending Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 祖師德，淮南觀察支使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shide was branch secretary of Huainan observation.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shide was branch secretary of Huainan observation.

sentences.zh: 父鄯，陜州法曹參軍。

translations.literal: His father Shan was legal officer of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shan was legal officer of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 扆，登進士第，其年從僖宗幸興元。

translations.literal: Yu passed the jinshi; that year he followed Emperor Xizong to Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed the jinshi. That year he followed Emperor Xizong to Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 九月，宰相韋昭度領鹽鐵，奏爲巡官。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chancellor Wei Zhaodu oversaw salt and iron and memorialized him as patrol officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chancellor Wei Zhaodu oversaw salt and iron and memorialized him as patrol officer.

sentences.zh: 明年，宰相孔緯奏直史館，得校書郎，尋丁母憂免。

translations.literal: The next year Chancellor Kong Wei memorialized him as direct historian of the History Office; he received proofreader and soon was dismissed on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Chancellor Kong Wei memorialized him as direct historian of the History Office. He received proofreader and soon was dismissed on mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 冬，召授藍田尉，直弘文館，遷左拾遺，兼集賢學士。

translations.literal: In winter he was summoned as magistrate of Lantian, direct scholar of the Hongwen Hall, promoted to Left Reminder, and concurrent academician of the Jixian Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he was summoned as magistrate of Lantian, direct scholar of the Hongwen Hall, promoted to Left Reminder, and concurrent academician of the Jixian Institute.

sentences.zh: 中丞柳玭奏改監察御史。

translations.literal: Vice censor Liu Pin memorialized to change him to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor Liu Pin memorialized to change him to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 大順二年三月，召充翰林學士，改屯田員外郎，賜緋。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Datong he was summoned as Hanlin academician, changed to vice director of the Bureau of Lands, and given crimson.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Datong he was summoned as Hanlin academician, changed to vice director of the Bureau of Lands, and given crimson.

sentences.zh: 景福元年，加祠部郎中、知制誥，二年元日朝賀，面賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingfu he was made director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafter of edicts; on New Year's Day court congratulations he was personally given gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingfu he was made director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and drafter of edicts. On New Year's Day court congratulations he was personally given gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 五月，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 扆文思敏速，初無思慮，揮翰如飛，文理俱愜，同舍服其能。

translations.literal: Yu's literary thought was swift; at first without deliberation he wrote as if flying—both pattern and reason satisfied, and colleagues in the same office admired his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's literary thought was swift. At first without deliberation he wrote as if flying—both pattern and reason satisfied, and colleagues in the same office admired his ability.

sentences.zh: 天子顧待特異。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven looked on him with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked on him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗金鑾作賦，命學士和，扆先成。

translations.literal: Once at Golden Hall he composed a fu and ordered the academicians to harmonize; Yu finished first.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Golden Hall he composed a fu and ordered the academicians to harmonize. Yu finished first.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而嗟挹之，曰：「朕聞貞元時有陸贄、吳通玄兄弟，能作內庭文書，後來絕不相繼。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and sighed in admiration: 'I have heard that in the Zhenyuan reign there were Lu Zhi and the brothers Wu Tongxuan, able to compose inner-court documents—afterward none succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and sighed in admiration. "I have heard that in the Zhenyuan reign there were Lu Zhi and the brothers Wu Tongxuan, able to compose inner-court documents—afterward none succeeded.

sentences.zh: 今吾得卿，斯文不墜矣。」

translations.literal: Now I have obtained you—this literature has not fallen.'
translations.idiomatic: Now I have obtained you—this literature has not fallen."

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，轉戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianning he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，改兵部，進階銀青光祿大夫、嘉興男、三百戸。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to war, advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Blue Light, Baron of Jiaxing with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was changed to war, advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Blue Light, Baron of Jiaxing with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，宣授學士承旨，尋改左丞。

translations.literal: In the third year, first month, he was proclaimed chief academician; soon changed to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, he was proclaimed chief academician. Soon he was changed to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，改戸部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year he was changed to vice minister of revenue and co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year he was changed to vice minister of revenue and co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 故事，三署除拜，有光署錢以宴舊僚，內署即無斯例。

translations.literal: By precedent, appointment in the three bureaus had 'bright bureau' money to feast old colleagues; the inner bureau had no such example.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, appointment in the three bureaus had 'bright bureau' money to feast old colleagues. The inner bureau had no such example.

sentences.zh: 扆拜輔相之月，送學士光院錢五百貫，特舉新例，內署榮之。

translations.literal: In the month Yu became assisting minister he sent five hundred strings of chief academician bright-court money, specially establishing a new precedent—the inner bureau was honored.
translations.idiomatic: In the month Yu became assisting minister he sent five hundred strings of chief academician bright-court money, specially establishing a new precedent. The inner bureau was honored.

sentences.zh: 八月，加中書侍郎、集賢殿大學士、判戸部事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was made vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, and in charge of revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made vice director of the Secretariat, Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall, and in charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 九月，覃王率師送徐彥若赴鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Prince of Tan led troops to escort Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Prince of Tan led troops to escort Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 師之起也，扆堅請曰：「播越之後，國步初集，不宜與近輔交惡，必爲他盜所窺。

translations.literal: When the army set out Yu firmly petitioned: 'After scattering in exile the state's steps are just gathered—it is not fitting to make enemies of nearby assistants; others will surely spy.
translations.idiomatic: When the army set out Yu firmly petitioned, "After scattering in exile the state's steps are just gathered—it is not fitting to make enemies of nearby assistants. Others will surely spy.

sentences.zh: 加以親王統兵，物議騰口，無益於事，只貽後患。」

translations.literal: Moreover with an imperial prince commanding troops public talk boils—no benefit to the affair, only leaving later trouble.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover with an imperial prince commanding troops public talk boils—no benefit to the affair, only leaving later trouble."

sentences.zh: 昭宗已發兵，怒扆沮議，是月十九日，責授硤州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhaozong had already sent troops and was angry that Yu obstructed discussion; on the nineteenth of that month he was demoted to Prefect of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong had already sent troops and was angry that Yu obstructed discussion. On the nineteenth of that month he was demoted to Prefect of Xia.

sentences.zh: 師出果敗，車駕出幸。

translations.literal: The army went out and indeed failed; the imperial carriage fled.
translations.idiomatic: The army went out and indeed failed. The imperial carriage fled.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，復授扆工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Yu was again made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Yu was again made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八月，轉兵部尚書，從昭宗自華還宮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to Minister of War and followed Zhaozong from Hua back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was transferred to Minister of War and followed Zhaozong from Hua back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，復拜中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he was again made vice director of the Secretariat and co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year he was again made vice director of the Secretariat and co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 四月，兼戸部尚書，進封吳郡開國公，食邑一千戸。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he concurrently was Minister of Revenue, advanced to Duke of Wu commandery with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he concurrently was Minister of Revenue, advanced to Duke of Wu commandery with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九月，轉門下侍郎、監修國史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 五月，進階特進，兼兵部尚書，加食邑五百戸。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was advanced to Special Advancement and concurrently Minister of War, with five hundred additional households in his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was advanced to Special Advancement and concurrently Minister of War, with five hundred additional households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 車駕自鳳翔還京，赦後諸道皆降詔書，獨鳳翔無詔。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned from Fengxiang to the capital, after the amnesty all circuits received edicts—only Fengxiang had none.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage returned from Fengxiang to the capital, after the amnesty all circuits received edicts—only Fengxiang had none.

sentences.zh: 扆奏曰：「鳳翔近在國門，責其心跡，罪實難容。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized: 'Fengxiang is near the capital gate; judging its heart and conduct, guilt is hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized, "Fengxiang is near the capital gate. Judging its heart and conduct, guilt is hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 然比來職貢無虧，朝廷未與之絕。

translations.literal: Yet lately its tribute duties were not lacking and the court has not broken with it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately its tribute duties were not lacking and the court has not broken with it.

sentences.zh: 一朝獨無詔命，示人不廣也。」

translations.literal: For one morning alone to have no edict shows the people a narrow mind.'
translations.idiomatic: For one morning alone to have no edict shows the people a narrow mind."

sentences.zh: 崔胤怒，奏貶扆沂王傅，分司東都，削階至正議大夫。

translations.literal: Cui Yin was angry and memorialized to demote Yu to Tutor of the Prince of Yi, commissioner at the Eastern Capital, and reduce his rank to Regular Grand Master of Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin was angry and memorialized to demote Yu to Tutor of the Prince of Yi, commissioner at the Eastern Capital, and reduce his rank to Regular Grand Master of Discussion.

sentences.zh: 居無何，崔胤誅，復授吏部尚書，階封如故。

translations.literal: Before long Cui Yin was executed; Yu was again made Minister of Civil Affairs with rank and fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cui Yin was executed. Yu was again made Minister of Civil Affairs with rank and fief as before.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗還洛。

translations.literal: He followed Zhaozong back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhaozong back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，昭宗遇弒。

translations.literal: That autumn Zhaozong was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhaozong was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，責授濮州司戸，與裴樞、崔遠、獨孤損等被害於滑州白馬驛，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he was demoted to registrar of Pu Prefecture and with Pei Shu, Cui Yuan, Dugu Sun and others was killed at Baima Post in Hua Prefecture, at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the next year he was demoted to registrar of Pu Prefecture and, with Pei Shu, Cui Yuan, Dugu Sun and others, was killed at Baima Post in Hua Prefecture, at age fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子璪，後爲緱氏令。

translations.literal: His son Can later served as magistrate of Gou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Can later served as magistrate of Gou.

sentences.zh: 柳璨，河東人。

translations.literal: Liu Can was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖子華。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Zihua.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Zihua.

sentences.zh: 祖公器，僕射公綽之再從弟也。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gongqi was a second cousin of Vice Director Gongchuo.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gongqi was a second cousin of Vice Director Gongchuo.

sentences.zh: 父遵。

translations.literal: His father Zun.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Zun.

sentences.zh: 璨少孤貧好學，僻居林泉。

translations.literal: Can was orphaned young and poor yet loved learning, dwelling secluded in forest springs.
translations.idiomatic: Can was orphaned young and poor yet loved learning, dwelling secluded in forest springs.

sentences.zh: 晝則采樵，夜則燃木葉以照書。

translations.literal: By day he gathered firewood; by night he burned tree leaves to light his books.
translations.idiomatic: By day he gathered firewood. By night he burned tree leaves to light his books.

sentences.zh: 性謇直，無緣飾。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and direct, without ornament.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was blunt and direct, without ornament.

sentences.zh: 宗人壁、玭，貴仕於朝，鄙璨樸鈍，不以諸宗齒之。

translations.literal: Clansmen Bi and Pin held noble office at court and despised Can as plain and dull, not ranking him among the clan by age.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen Bi and Pin held noble office at court and despised Can as plain and dull, not ranking him among the clan by age.

sentences.zh: 光化中，登進士第。

translations.literal: In the Guanghua reign he passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guanghua reign he passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 尤精《漢史》，魯國顏蕘深重之。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in Han history; Yan Qiao of Lu deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially expert in Han history. Yan Qiao of Lu deeply valued him.

sentences.zh: 蕘爲中書舍人，判史館，引爲直學士。

translations.literal: Qiao was Vice Director of the Secretariat and judged the History Office; he recruited Can as direct academician.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was Vice Director of the Secretariat and judged the History Office. He recruited Can as direct academician.

sentences.zh: 璨以劉子玄所撰《史通》譏駁經史過當，璨紀子玄之失，別爲十卷，號《柳氏釋史》，學者伏其優贍。

translations.literal: Can, because Liu Zixuan's Comprehensive Mirror criticized the classics and histories excessively, enumerated Zixuan's faults in another ten scrolls titled Mr. Liu's Explication of History; scholars submitted to his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Can, because Liu Zixuan's Comprehensive Mirror criticized the classics and histories excessively, enumerated Zixuan's faults in another ten scrolls titled Mr. Liu's Explication of History. Scholars submitted to his erudition.

sentences.zh: 遷左拾遺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 公卿朝野，托爲箋奏，時譽日洽。

translations.literal: Nobles at court and in the wild entrusted him with letters and memorials; his reputation daily spread.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles at court and in the wild entrusted him with letters and memorials. His reputation daily spread.

sentences.zh: 以其博奧，目爲「柳篋子」。

translations.literal: Because of his vast learning he was called 'Liu the Document Case.'
translations.idiomatic: Because of his vast learning he was called 'Liu the Document Case.'

sentences.zh: 昭宗好文，初寵待李谿頗學。

translations.literal: Zhaozong loved literature and at first favored Li Xi for learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong loved literature and at first favored Li Xi for learning.

sentences.zh: 洎谿不得其死，心常惜之，求文士似谿者。

translations.literal: When Xi met his death the heart always regretted it and sought literary men resembling Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi met his death the heart always regretted it and sought literary men resembling Xi.

sentences.zh: 或薦璨高才，召見，試以詩什，甚喜。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Can's high talent; summoned to audience he was tested with poems and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Someone recommended Can's high talent. Summoned to audience he was tested with poems and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 無幾，召爲翰林學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 崔胤得罪前一日，召璨入內殿草制敕。

translations.literal: The day before Cui Yin's guilt he summoned Can to the inner hall to draft edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The day before Cui Yin's guilt he summoned Can to the inner hall to draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 胤死之日，既夕，璨自內出，前驅傳呼相公來。

translations.literal: On the day Yin died, at evening Can came out from within; runners ahead cried that the chancellor was coming.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yin died, at evening Can came out from within. Runners ahead cried that the chancellor was coming.

sentences.zh: 人未見制敕，莫測所以。

translations.literal: People had not yet seen the edict and could not fathom why.
translations.idiomatic: People had not yet seen the edict and could not fathom why.

sentences.zh: 翌日對學士，上謂之曰：「朕以柳璨奇特，似可獎任。

translations.literal: The next day facing the academicians the emperor said to them: 'I find Liu Can extraordinary and worthy of reward and employment.
translations.idiomatic: The next day facing the academicians the emperor said to them, "I find Liu Can extraordinary and worthy of reward and employment.

sentences.zh: 若令預政事，宜授何官？」

translations.literal: If he is to participate in government, what office should be granted?'
translations.idiomatic: If he is to participate in government, what office should be granted?"

sentences.zh: 承旨張文蔚曰：「陛下拔用賢能，固不拘資級。

translations.literal: Chief academician Zhang Wenwei said: 'Your Majesty elevates talent and ability and is not bound by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Chief academician Zhang Wenwei said, "Your Majesty elevates talent and ability and is not bound by seniority.

sentences.zh: 恩命高下，出自聖懷。

translations.literal: The height of grace comes from the sacred heart.
translations.idiomatic: The height of grace comes from the sacred heart.

sentences.zh: 若循兩省遷轉，拾遺超等入起居郎，臨大位，非宜也。」

translations.literal: If following the two departments' promotions—from Reminder surpassing rank to Recorder—nearing the great post, it is not fitting.'
translations.idiomatic: If following the two departments' promotions—from Reminder surpassing rank to Recorder—nearing the great post, it is not fitting."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「超至諫議大夫可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Promoted to Remonstrating Official—is that acceptable?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Promoted to Remonstrating Official—is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 文蔚曰：「此命甚愜。」

translations.literal: Wenwei said: 'This appointment is very satisfying.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei said, "This appointment is very satisfying."

sentences.zh: 即以諫議大夫平章事，改中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Remonstrating Official he became co-chancellor and was changed to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon with Remonstrating Official he became co-chancellor and was changed to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 任人之速，古無茲例。

translations.literal: The speed of appointing men—antiquity had no such example.
translations.idiomatic: The speed of appointing men—antiquity had no such example.

sentences.zh: 同列裴樞、獨孤損、崔遠皆宿素名德，遽與璨同列，意微輕之，璨深蓄怨。

translations.literal: Fellow ministers Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, and Cui Yuan were all long-standing in fame and virtue; suddenly to rank with Can—they inwardly slighted him and Can deeply nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow ministers Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, and Cui Yuan were all long-standing in fame and virtue. Suddenly to rank with Can—they inwardly slighted him and Can deeply nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛，諸司內使、宿衛將佐，皆朱全忠腹心也，璨皆將迎，接之以恩，厚相交結，故當時權任皆歸之。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, inner bureau attendants and guard officers were all Zhu Quanzhong's trusted men; Can all went to meet them, treating them with kindness and forming deep ties—therefore power at the time all returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, inner bureau attendants and guard officers were all Zhu Quanzhong's trusted men. Can all went to meet them, treating them with kindness and forming deep ties—therefore power at the time all returned to him.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，西北長星竟天，掃太微、文昌、帝座諸宿，全忠方謀篡代。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year a long comet in the northwest crossed the heavens, sweeping the lodges of Supreme Palace, Administrative Star, and Imperial Seat; Quanzhong was just plotting usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year a long comet in the northwest crossed the heavens, sweeping the lodges of Supreme Palace, Administrative Star, and Imperial Seat. Quanzhong was just plotting usurpation.

sentences.zh: 而妖星謫見，占者云：「君臣俱災，宜刑殺以應天變。」

translations.literal: The demonic star appeared as reprimand; diviners said: 'Ruler and ministers both suffer disaster—punishment and killing should answer Heaven's change.'
translations.idiomatic: The demonic star appeared as reprimand. Diviners said, "Ruler and ministers both suffer disaster—punishment and killing should answer Heaven's change."

sentences.zh: 蔣玄暉、張廷範謀殺衣冠宿望難制者，璨即首疏素所不快者三十餘人，相次誅殺。

translations.literal: Jiang Xuanhui and Zhang Tingfan plotted to kill eminent robes and longstanding repute hard to control; Can was first to memorialize those he had long disliked, more than thirty persons, who were executed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xuanhui and Zhang Tingfan plotted to kill eminent robes and longstanding repute hard to control. Can was first to memorialize those he had long disliked, more than thirty persons, who were executed in succession.

sentences.zh: 班行爲之一空，冤聲載路。

translations.literal: The ranks were emptied at once; cries of injustice filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The ranks were emptied at once. Cries of injustice filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 傷害既甚，朱全忠心惡之。

translations.literal: The harm was already extreme and Zhu Quanzhong detested it in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The harm was already extreme and Zhu Quanzhong detested it in his heart.

sentences.zh: 會全忠授九錫，蔣玄暉等別陳意見。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong was granted the nine bestowments, Jiang Xuanhui and others separately stated other views.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong was granted the nine bestowals, Jiang Xuanhui and others separately stated other views.

sentences.zh: 王殷至大梁，誣玄暉等通導宮掖，欲興復李氏。

translations.literal: Wang Yin reached Daliang and slandered Xuanhui and others for communicating with the inner palace, wishing to restore the Li house.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin reached Daliang and slandered Xuanhui and others for communicating with the inner palace, wishing to restore the Li house.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒，捕廷範，令河南聚眾，五軍分裂之，兼誅璨，臨刑呼曰：「負國賊柳璨，死其宜矣！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong was angry, arrested Tingfan, ordered Henan to gather the crowd, and the five armies dismembered him; Can was also executed. At execution he cried: 'The traitor to the state Liu Can—death is fitting!'
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was angry, arrested Tingfan, ordered Henan to gather the crowd, and the five armies dismembered him. Can was also executed. At execution he cried, "The traitor to the state Liu Can—death is fitting!"

sentences.zh: 初，璨遷洛後，累兼戸部尚書、守司空，進階光祿大夫、鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Can moved to Luoyang he cumulatively was Minister of Revenue and acting Minister of Works, advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and commissioner of salt and iron transport.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Can moved to Luoyang he cumulatively was Minister of Revenue and acting Minister of Works, advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and commissioner of salt and iron transport.

sentences.zh: 其弟瑀、瑊坐璨笞死。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Yu and Jian were implicated and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Yu and Jian were implicated and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：嗚呼！

translations.literal: The historian says: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Alas!

sentences.zh: 李氏之失馭也，孛沴之氣紛如，仁義之徒殆盡。

translations.literal: When the Li house lost the reins, baleful vapors swarmed; men of benevolence and righteousness were nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Li house lost the reins, baleful vapors swarmed. Men of benevolence and righteousness were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 狐鳴鴟嘯，瓦解土崩。

translations.literal: Foxes cried and owls shrieked; dissolution was like crumbling earth.
translations.idiomatic: Foxes cried and owls shrieked. Dissolution was like crumbling earth.

sentences.zh: 帶河礪嶽之門，寂無琨、逖；

translations.literal: In gates bound by river and mountain oaths there were none like Kun or Ti;
translations.idiomatic: In gates bound by river and mountain oaths there were none like Kun or Ti.

sentences.zh: 奮挺揭竿之類，唯效敦、玄。

translations.literal: Among those who raised poles and banners only Dun and Xuan were imitated.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who raised poles and banners only Dun and Xuan were imitated.

sentences.zh: 手未舍於棘矜，心已萌於問鼎。

translations.literal: Hands had not yet left the thornwood spear; hearts already sprouted the intent to seize the tripod.
translations.idiomatic: Hands had not yet left the thornwood spear. Hearts already sprouted the intent to seize the tripod.

sentences.zh: 加以囂浮士子，阘茸鯫儒。

translations.literal: Moreover arrogant floating scholars and incompetent petty pedants
translations.idiomatic: Moreover arrogant floating scholars and incompetent petty pedants

sentences.zh: 昧管、葛濟時之才，無王、謝扶顛之業，邀功射利，陷族喪邦。

translations.literal: lacked the timely talent of Guan and Ge, lacked the sustaining work of Wang and Xie, sought merit and shot for profit, and ruined clans and lost the state.
translations.idiomatic: lacked the timely talent of Guan and Ge, lacked the sustaining work of Wang and Xie, sought merit and shot for profit, and ruined clans and lost the state.

sentences.zh: 濬、緯養虎於前，胤、璨剝廬於後。

translations.literal: Jun and Wei reared tigers before; Yin and Can stripped the hut behind.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Wei reared tigers before. Yin and Can stripped the hut behind.

sentences.zh: 逐徐、薛於瘴海，置綮、朴於巖廊。

translations.literal: They drove Xu and Xue to the malarial sea and placed Qi and Pu in the rock corridor.
translations.idiomatic: They drove Xu and Xue to the malarial sea and placed Qi and Pu in the rock corridor.

sentences.zh: 殿廷有哭制之夫，輔弼走破輿之黨。

translations.literal: In the hall court were men who wept at edict proclamation; assisting ministers fled with the faction that smashed the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall court were men who wept at edict proclamation. Assisting ministers fled with the faction that smashed the carriage.

sentences.zh: 九疇既紊，百怪斯呈。

translations.literal: The nine fields were already disordered; a hundred portents then appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The nine fields were already disordered. A hundred portents then appeared.

sentences.zh: 木將朽而蠹蠍生，厲既篤而夔魖見。

translations.literal: Wood about to rot breeds worms and scorpions; sickness already deep summons demons and ogres.
translations.idiomatic: Wood about to rot breeds worms and scorpions. Sickness already deep summons demons and ogres.

sentences.zh: 妖徒若此，亡國宜然。

translations.literal: Wicked followers like this—state extinction was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked followers like this—state extinction was fitting.

sentences.zh: 何必長星，更臨衰運？

translations.literal: Why must a long comet again descend on a declining fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Why must a long comet again descend on a declining fortune?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：蕭召、朱玫，孔符、張濬，身世罹殃，邦家起釁。

translations.literal: Praise says: Xiao summoned and Zhu Mei, Kong talisman and Zhang Jun—bodies and lives met calamity, the state raised strife.
translations.idiomatic: Praise says: Xiao summoned and Zhu Mei, Kong talisman and Zhang Jun—bodies and lives met calamity, the state raised strife.

sentences.zh: 如木斯蠹，自潰於中。

translations.literal: Like wood with worms, it collapsed from within.
translations.idiomatic: Like wood with worms, it collapsed from within.

sentences.zh: 抵巇侮亂，安責伏戎。

translations.literal: Meeting peril and insulting disorder—how can one blame those who subdued the war?
translations.idiomatic: Meeting peril and insulting disorder—how can one blame those who subdued the war?
